Shakira, Pique return to court over children visit arrangements
items.description: Pop star Shakira and her former partner, retired Spanish footballer Gerard Pique, appeared at a Barcelona court on Tuesday to review visitation arrangements for their two children, with the singer seeking changes to limit their travel between the US and Spain. The Colombian singer has asked for fewer short transatlantic trips by their sons between Miami, where they live with her, and Barcelona, where Pique lives, according to a statement from her legal team. She argues that frequent travel could affect their emotional, physical and academic wellbeing, her representatives said. Under her proposal, Pique would travel to Miami during shorter school holidays, allowing the children to spend more time in their home environment and maintain their routines. The request is not intended to reduce the amount of time the children spend with their father, they added. Shakira, 49, and Pique, 39, began their relationship in 2011 and have two boys, Milan, born in 2013, and Sasha, born in 2015. The couple, who lived mainly in Barcelona during their relationship, announced their separation in June 2022 after more than a decade together. They reached an agreement over custody and visitation arrangements several months later, after which the “Hips Don’t Lie” singer moved to Miami with the kids. Pique, who played for Barcelona and Spain before retiring from professional football in 2022, has regular periods with his sons each month as well as during school holidays. Shakira is currently in Madrid for the final leg of a global tour, with 13 concerts scheduled between September 18 and October 12. She added an extra date on Monday. She began her “Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran” world tour in February 2025, taking its name from her album of the same title. The album includes “Bzrp Music Sessions, Vol. 53”, her global hit collaboration with Argentine producer Bizarrap, which referenced her split from Pique. items.title: Scrap NYSC or let participants serve in their states – NAPTAN tells FG
items.description: By Adesina Wahab Parents under the aegis of the National Parent Teacher Association of Nigeria, NAPTAN, have called on the Federal Government to scrap the National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, Scheme or allow participants to observe it in their states of origin. This, according to the association, has become imperative following the soft targets members and prospective members of the scheme have become in the hands of criminal elements who kidnap them. Speaking in an interview with Vanguard on Tuesday, the Chairman, Board of Trustees of NAPTAN, Chief Adeolu Ogunbanjo, expressed sadness that the scheme is being turned to a curse rather than a blessing to parents and participants. “Parents are not happy with the incessant abduction and kidnap of our children going for the NYSC scheme. This must stop. Our children that we suffer to train in school should not be seen as soft targets by criminal elements such as kidnappers. They are not items of merchandise that somebody will be haggling about how much to pay for their release. “There is no doubt that the idea behind the setting up of the scheme is good, but the realities of today are not fully supporting that. Let us look at the percentage of parents who can say their wards or children should go by air to their places of deployment; it may be less than five per cent. It means no matter how long the distance, more than 95 per cent of corps members travel by road to their states of deployment. “One can imagine the various hazards on the road, even the state of our highways. Highways that are prone to accidents. Is the risk worth it? We are suggesting that the government should let corps members serve in their states of origin. At least, Yoruba elders say that your father’s house cannot be a threat to you. “Even the condition under which most corps members serve is not good enough. We call for the improvement in the various orientation camps. Graduates should not be treated as animals. Most employers don’t even provide the corps members basic things for their comfort. They don’t give them accommodation. “Regarding the corps members that are being held captive by abductors, please all hands must be on deck to ensure their quick and safe return. When the kidnappers are demanding millions of naira, where do they expect the parents to raise such money from? Parents who could not afford to send their wards by plane to those places,” he stated. Ogunbanjo prayed for the quick release of the 19 corps members being help-captive in Imo State. items.title: Kidal : l’armée malienne reprend le contrôle de la ville
items.description: L'armee malienne a repris, ce mardi 6 octobre, le controle de Kidal, dans le nord du Mali. Les Forces armees maliennes sont entrees dans la ville sans resistance. Ce retour intervient plus de cinq mois apres la prise de Kidal par le Front de liberation de l'Azawad (FLA), allie au Groupe de soutien a l'islam et aux musulmans (JNIM). Plusieurs sources securitaires confirment cette entree des Fama a Kidal.Les forces armees maliennes poursuivent leur deploiement a l'interieur de la ville, jusque-la controlee par le FLA. Dans un communique, le mouvement arme, le Front de liberation de l'azawad FLA, affirme avoir decide de se retirer de la ville afin de preserver la vie des rares populations civiles qui y sont encore presentes. Fief des groupes rebelles depuis 2012, Kidal avait ete reprise par l'armee malienne en 2023. Les FAMa avaient cependant perdu le controle de la ville le 25 avril 2026, a la suite d'attaques coordonnees de la coalition FLA-JNIM. Une reprise dans un contexte regional particulier La reprise de Kidal intervient alors que le Mali et l'Algerie renouent leur cooperation. Elle intervient egalement quelques semaines apres la declaration du president de la Transition, qui avait affirme que le pays restait ouvert au dialogue. Cette nouvelle evolution militaire pourrait-elle modifier les rapports de force en amont d'une eventuelle reprise des negociations ? La suite des evenements permettra de le determiner. items.title: NYSC Kidnap: Families lament Oyo govt’s silence; ‘We’re on top of situation’ – Ministry
items.description: By Adeola Badru Families of would-be National Youth Service Corps, NYSC, member abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in Imo State have expressed anguish and frustration over what they described as the failure of the Oyo State government to directly reach out to them and reassure them of efforts to secure their children’s safe return. Read Also: ‘Why we couldn’t rescue Air Force aircraft crash victims’ – lgbokoda residents The affected families said they had been left to grapple with fear, uncertainty and emotional trauma following the abduction of the prospective corps members. Some parents alleged that no representative of the state government had contacted them to provide information or offer reassurances since the incident. The development has heightened anxiety among the families, particularly as they continue to await the safe return of their loved ones amid reports that the abductors are demanding ransom. ‘This hurts as a father’ One of the affected parents, Mr Femi Adewale, 53, a public servant and father of Feyisayo, one of the abducted prospective corps members, said the uncertainty surrounding his daughter’s whereabouts had left the family devastated. Adewale, in an interview with Vanguard on Tuesday, said the family had been living in fear, particularly because they had not received direct communication from the state government, explaining what was being done to secure the release of the abducted corps members. He said: “As a father, this is extremely painful. You send your child out believing that she is going to serve her country and build her future. Only for her to be kidnapped on the way. “Since this happened, every telephone call puts us on edge because we do not know what news we are going to hear. “What we expect from the government is reassurance. We want to know that the government is doing everything within its power to bring our children back safely. We should not be left to face this kind of situation alone.” Adewale appealed to the authorities to intensify efforts to rescue the abducted corps members, saying the families were already under enormous emotional pressure. He added: “These are young Nigerians who have gone out to serve their country. They are not criminals. They are our children. The government must do everything possible to ensure that they come back alive and safely to their families.” ‘What my daughter told me’ – Mrs Oyeyemi Similarly, Mrs Sade Oyeyemi, 51, whose only daughter, Kemisola, was among those abducted, said her family had been thrown into deep anguish after hearing the condition of her daughter during a conversation permitted by the kidnappers. Oyeyemi said her daughter, who was allegedly subjected to severe torture and sustained injuries, was only allowed to speak with the family briefly, during which she told them that the abductors were becoming increasingly impatient over the ransom. According to the distraught mother, her daughter warned that the situation could become fatal if the kidnappers’ demands were not met. She said while crying, “Kemisola is my only daughter. Imagine what it means for a mother to hear her only child crying and telling you that she is being tortured and injured. There is no mother who can hear that and remain calm. “When she was allowed to speak with us, we could hear the pain in her voice. She told us that they were not joking with the ransom, and that they could kill them if their patience was exhausted. “Since then, I have not been myself. I am constantly afraid that something terrible could happen to my daughter.” Oyeyemi appealed to the government and security agencies to intervene urgently, stressing that the families were not asking for anything beyond the safe return of their children. “We are appealing to the government to help us. These children have parents who love them and families waiting for them. We cannot afford to lose them. Whatever needs to be done to bring them back alive should be done urgently. “I am a mother and this is my only daughter. I cannot imagine my life without her. We need the government to talk to us, tell us what is happening and assure us that everything possible is being done to rescue our children.” Oyo govt reacts Reacting to the assertion, the Oyo State Commissioner for Information, Mr. Dotun Oyelade, said the state government was not indifferent to the plight of the affected families, insisting that the Ministry of Education was handling the situation. Oyelade, responding to questions on the allegation that the government had not reached out to the affected families, said: “To the best of my knowledge, the Ministry of Education is on top of the situation.” According to him, efforts were being made to establish contact with the families, adding that he was aware that government officials had sought their addresses and contacted relevant local government authorities to assist in locating them. “The commissioner told me they are reaching out to them. I knew when they were searching for their address and asking some local governments to help track them,“ he said. Oyelade, however, acknowledged that he was aware of reports that representatives had visited the Olubadan, while stressing that the Ministry of Education was taking steps to address the situation. “We only heard that they went to the Olubadan, but not to the state government. I know that the Ministry of Education is doing something about it,” he said. items.description: Prosecutors are still investigating the six Matsda2sh journalists who are being held in remand detention for 15 days, effective from the day they were brought before the Supreme State Security Prosecution, according to Hossam Bahgat, the director of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are leading the defense counsel representing the journalists. Prosecutors largely repeated the same line of questioning the journalists faced in the first round of interrogations, focusing on the platform’s editorial policy and their professional backgrounds, according to lawyers informed of the investigations. Journalists from the independent fact-checking platform had previously been held at National Security Agency premises for almost an entire week, following the arrest campaign that targeted six of the outlet’s team members. After several of the journalists described being forced to record false “confessions” on camera and being subjected to torture at the hands of the National Security Agency officers, the Journalists Syndicate published a statement on Monday night saying its members had decided “unanimously” to file a complaint with the public prosecutor regarding the charges. Although prosecutors had decided that one of the journalists should be sent for a forensic medical examination to document signs of torture, he is yet to be brought in for medical examination, according to lawyers informed of the investigation who spoke to Mada Masr. One lawyer told Mada Masr he had learned that a heightened security presence was observed on Tuesday morning around the Egyptian Forensic Medicine Authority at Zeinhom morgue, which he said could indicate that the journalists may be sent for the examination in the coming hours. Another lawyer said that the 24-hour delay in conducting the examination may have caused the visible signs of torture to fade beyond forensic recognition. The Interior Ministry denied on Monday that the Matsda2sh journalists, whom it described as Muslim Brotherhood elements, were tortured or mistreated. It said that the torture claims were merely “echoed in the Journalists Syndicate statement and on some pages affiliated with the terrorist Muslim Brotherhood” and described the claims as an attempt by the defendants to “evade the charges attributed to them.” In its Monday night statement, the syndicate board stressed its commitment to legally defending all practicing journalists, regardless of whether or not they have syndicate membership, citing the syndicate law, which requires that journalists already be practicing the profession as a prerequisite to membership. The Interior Ministry had differentiated, in its announcement of the journalists’ arrest, between those who have syndicate membership and those who do not. The syndicate issued its statement following an emergency board meeting on Monday evening that ran for over four hours and was marked by a tense atmosphere, a syndicate source told Mada Masr. Tensions arose over disputes regarding the syndicate’s responsibility to provide legal defense for the five journalists who are not members and the need for action in response to their accounts of torture. Several members of the syndicate’s general assembly gathered outside the meeting hall while the discussions were underway, chanting for the council to extend the syndicate’s defense to all detained journalists, whether or not they are members, saying “all six are our colleagues,” “you who are silent, speak up and don’t be afraid,” “freedom for Matsda2sh” and “no to torture.” The syndicate said in its statement that it had submitted memoranda to prosecutors clarifying the legal basis of their intervention in defense of all the practicing journalists. The syndicate board also indicated the Matsda2sh journalists’ commitment to regularizing their employment status under Egyptian law as evidence of their good intentions, noting they had taken legal steps to document their employment status in 2023 following an incident in which three of the platform’s team were briefly arrested and their names publicly circulated, while a fourth was taken into custody for two days before he was released following the syndicate’s intervention. None of the platform’s team were charged at the time. The post Syndicate submits prosecution complaint regarding Matsda2sh journalists’ torture, Interior Ministry denies claims first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Man City 115 charges: Sheikh Mansour could sell club if appeal fails – Reports
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour could sell the club if its appeal against the Premier League’s guilty verdict fails, according to leading UAE expert Christopher M. Davidson. Speaking in an interview with The Athletic, Davidson, a renowned Middle East analyst and author of Abu Dhabi: Oil & Beyond, believes Abu Dhabi’s ruling family would feel too “embarrassed and disgraced” to retain ownership under a tainted reputation in England. The Premier League last week confirmed that an independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of its financial rules over a nine-season period from 2009/10 to 2017/18. The commission found that City had arranged “sham” contracts with commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs, while also finding the club guilty of three of four groups of alleged failures to cooperate with the Premier League’s investigation. City have denied wrongdoing and appealed against the verdict, insisting that the commission’s findings contain material errors of law, principle and fact. However, Davidson believes an unsuccessful appeal could change the position of City’s owners. “Once there’s some time to digest this, my feeling would be that they would extricate themselves,” he told The Athletic. “I think primarily it would be seen from a political and cultural aspect. The ruling family of Abu Dhabi would feel that they had been embarrassed and disgraced by this ruling, and the best way of moving forward would be to sell now to cut the losses, as it were, rather than allow this to be a festering, lingering problem where the ownership of their club would be forever tainted in England. “I can’t see any scenario where they would continue.” Davidson’s assessment, however, contrasts with comments made by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in June, when he said there was “no intention to sell” the club and described Manchester City and the wider City Football Group as “jewels” that are not sold. “Manchester City and this group within the football world is a pinnacle and these sorts of jewels you don’t sell,” Al Mubarak remarked earlier this year. However, Davidson maintained that an upheld guilty verdict on appeal would alter that calculus completely, forcing Abu Dhabi to protect its broader global standing by severing ties with the Etihad outfit. ‘I leave in peace’ — Messi says ahead of final Argentina game
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Lionel Messi has said he is leaving the Argentina national team “in peace” as he prepares to make his final appearance for the country against Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires on Tuesday. “The moment has arrived. I leave in peace, I gave it my all,” Messi said, according to football journalist Fabrizio Romano. “This shirt was my dream, my pride, and my life for years,” the Argentina captain added. Messi also thanked the supporters who have followed him throughout his 21-year international career. “Thank you for loving me so much, thank you for your support. I will always carry you with me,” he said. The 39-year-old announced his retirement from international football in August, bringing an end to a career that saw him become Argentina’s all-time leading scorer with 125 goals in 207 appearances. His final game against Benin Republic will be his 208th for the Albiceleste and will bring an emotional conclusion to a journey that began in 2005. Messi endured painful defeats with Argentina before eventually leading the country to Copa América triumphs in 2021 and 2024 and the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. The farewell match has been billed as a celebration of Messi’s extraordinary contribution to Argentine football, with more than 85,000 fans expected at the Monumental. The Argentine Football Association has also invited members of the 2022 World Cup-winning squad and their families for the occasion. Argentina will wear a special commemorative kit for the occasion, while Messi will wear the iconic No. 10 shirt for the final time. The AFA had previously confirmed that no other player would wear the number before his farewell. After Tuesday’s farewell, Messi will continue his club career with Inter Miami in the Majos League Soccer (MLS). The post ‘I leave in peace’ — Messi says ahead of final Argentina game appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan successfully tests launch of extended version of Fatah-IV cruise missile: ISPR
items.description: Pakistan conducted a successful test launch of the indigenously developed extended version of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile, the military’s media wing said in a statement on Tuesday. In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said, “Equipped with advanced avionics and state-of-the-art navigational aids, the weapon system is capable of engaging targets at extended ranges with high precision and lethality.” “The test also validated additional technical parameters of various sub-systems incorporated for improved accuracy and enhanced survivability,” it added. According to the statement, the launch was witnessed by senior officers from the Pakistan Army along with scientists and engineers of the developing agency. It added that President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and all service chiefs commended the successful test and “appreciated the technical prowess, dedication and commitment of all those who contributed towards achieving this milestone”. In May, the Army Rocket Force Command conducted the successful test fire of the Fatah-IV ground-launched cruise missile. A month earlier, the Army Rocket Force Command had also conducted the successful training launch of the Fateh-II missile system. The same month, the Pakistan Navy successfully fired a locally developed anti-ship ballistic missile to engage targets at an extended range. In September 2025, the Pakistan Army had also successfully conducted the training launch of the Fatah-IV cruise missile at a range of 750 kilometres.

items.title: Woman ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​​‍⁠‍‍​⁠‌​pleads guilty to assisting ISWAP members to keep arms, ammunition
items.description: A woman, Sumaiya Abubakar, on Tuesday admitted to rendering support to members of the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) in Nasarawa State. Sumaiya, who was arraigned before Justice Salim Ibrahim of the Federal High Court in Abuja, pleaded guilty to count two of the charges preferred against her by the Federal Government. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Federal Government filed the charge against Sumaiya, the sole defendant in the case. Rotimi Oyedepo, SAN, the Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, in the charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/418/2026, accused the defendant of terrorism-related offences. In count two, where she pleaded guilty, Sumaiya, who hails from Shuwari village, Kukawa Local Government Area (LGA) of Borno, was alleged to have committed the offence sometime in 2024 at Shinge area, Lafiya LGA of Nasarawa State. She was alleged to have knowingly rendered support to members of the ISWAP by helping to keep arms and ammunition. The offence, the prosecution said, is contrary to and punishable under Section 13 of the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act, 2022. When the case was called, M.A. Oladunjoye, who appeared for the Federal Government, informed the court that the matter was scheduled for Sumaiya’s arraignment. E.G. Itodo, the defence lawyer, did not object. When the counts were read to Sumaiya, she pleaded not guilty to count one but pleaded guilty to count two. Oladunjoye then prayed the court to convict the defendant in the count she had pleaded guilty to. The lawyer then applied to withdraw count one, where the defendant pleaded not guilty to. Itodo did not oppose the application for withdrawal, and Justice Ibrahim struck out count one from the charge. But the judge observed that there was a need for the prosecuting counsel to review the facts before the defendant is convicted. Justice Ibrahim therefore adjourned the matter until Oct. 14 for review of facts on count two, which Sumaiya pleaded guilty to. He equally ordered that the defendant should be remanded in the custody of the Department of State Services (DSS) pending the next adjourned date. items.title: Ghanaians in their 30s and 50s dying from heart disease without knowing – Cardiothoracic Centre
items.description: Cardiovascular disease is increasingly claiming the lives of Ghanaians at younger ages, with the Director of the National Cardiothoracic Centre, Dr Kow Entsua-Mensah, warning that many of the deaths could be prevented. He said people in their 30s and 50s are dying from heart-related conditions, with some unaware they have the disease until they suffer serious complications. “A lot of people are working with a disease in their bodies, but because they don’t check, they cannot find it,” Dr Entsua-Mensah said. He was speaking during this year’s World Heart Day activities held at the Efua Sutherland Children’s Park under the theme, “Heart Disease Can Hide in Plain Sight. Don’t Miss a Beat.” Dr Entsua-Mensah said Ghana’s preparedness to respond to cardiovascular emergencies needed improvement, making prevention and early detection particularly important. “Our preparation as a nation for the management of emergencies can be better as it is,” he said. He urged Ghanaians to take greater responsibility for their heart health by exercising regularly, eating healthier meals, getting adequate sleep and undergoing routine health checks. “We want to focus on the prevention,” he said, stressing that people should not wait until a health emergency occurs before seeking medical attention. The Director also called for greater public awareness of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and basic emergency response, saying ordinary citizens can help save lives when they know how to respond when someone collapses or stops breathing. “You don’t have to be a health person,” he said. “Anybody who gets the opportunity should learn how to respond when somebody collapses, somebody is unconscious or somebody stops breathing.” As part of the World Heart Day activities, the National Cardiothoracic Centre partnered with St John Ambulance to provide emergency response training. Dr Entsua-Mensah said stronger prevention, early detection and public knowledge of emergency response could help reduce avoidable deaths from cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Emeritus Professor Kwame Akon Ninsin: The man who mentored a department
items.description: On October 1, 2026, the Department of Political Science, University of Ghana, gathered to honour one of its pillars – Emeritus Professor Kwame Akon Ninsin. Political scientist, statesman, avowed Nkrumahist, activist. True to his influence, the room was full. Emeritus Professor Atsu Ayee and many faculty members were present. So were leading civil society figures including media freedom advocate Prof. Kwame Karikari and Dr Emmanuel Akwetey, founder of the Institute for Democratic Governance (IDEG). Speaker after speaker rose, but a clear picture emerged of who Ninsin was. The Trinity Who Built a Department Former Speaker of Parliament, Prof. Mike Oquaye, who was both taught by Ninsin and taught in the Department, described the trinity that built Political Science. “Folson founded the Department, Kofi Drah nourished it, and Kwame Ninsin became Emeritus of what they established.” He remembered Ninsin’s eye for talent, his conspiratorial discussions about how to grow the Department, and the period around 1988 that gave them the chance for a second wave. “We published and flourished. Morally, he stood above what was required of a lecturer. He promoted a system of collegiality and conviviality.” Mr F. K. Drah, the grandfather of the Department who joined in 1969 and led it for two decades, spoke of a friendship so deep that people wondered who taught who. He recalled barbering the young Ninsin. He also noted Ninsin’s deliberate mentoring of women scholars – Dr Beatrice Allah-Mensah, Dr Maame Gyekye-Johnson and Prof. Rosina Foli among them. “I am sad because we no longer enjoy his company,” Mr Drah said, “but it is not for us to determine. God the Creator knows where He wants him to be.” Provost of the College of Humanities, Prof. Joseph Yaro, summed it up: Political Science is one of the best departments in the University because men like Ninsin built it. The Teacher Who Was Not a Populist If the first part was about institution-building, the second was about teaching. Prof. Kwame Boafo-Arthur, a former Head of Department who was taught by Ninsin, remembered his Marxism and his bluntness. Ninsin was not a populist lecturer chasing student popularity. “The course outline is your baby,” he would insist. Getting a C is also a grade. He pushed his students to think beyond the classroom, even advising Boafo-Arthur to look for an income-generating asset – advice that sent him to Nigeria for a while. Prof. Abeeku Essuman-Johnson recalled that Ninsin visited him at home when he missed classes after flight challenges from Nigeria. He often ran errands for Ninsin. Prof. Atsu Ayee, who clarified that Ninsin arrived when he was in his final year, said they later bonded deeply as colleagues navigating academia together. Kwesi Jonah, who straddled the Department and IDEG, described his relationship with Ninsin as father and son. They shared an office where they spent hours gossiping about national affairs, a habit that continued at IDEG and culminated in Ninsin’s last book, The Corrupt Elites: Anatomy of Power and Wealth in Ghana. He was not just an office academic; he visited staff at home. The Activist Beyond the Classroom The tributes also remembered Ninsin the public intellectual. Prof. S.K.B. Asante Danso-Boafo, now Secretary to Cabinet, credited Ninsin for helping publish his controversial book on former President Rawlings – an act of academic freedom. Dr Emmanuel Akwetey recalled Ninsin’s alarm about state capture of Parliament. In 2007, worried whether Ghana was a tribe or a nation, Ninsin wrote a paper to address the nation. That intervention grew into a conference drawing scholars from across the continent. He worked extensively on elections to prevent violence and served as Director of Research at IDEG. My Last Student I was his friend and his last MPhil student. I first met him as an undergraduate at a lecture on Darfur organised by the Forum for Student Affairs, a campus group he founded. As a novice, he cut my teeth in academic writing. As a member of the Young Pioneers Movement – a youth movement of which my grandfather, the late Z. B. Shardow, was Director and a prominent member of the Convention People’s Party – he had high expectations of me. He was very fast with drafts and never happy with my slow moments. He would say, “I was expecting you to work like your grandfather, Z.B. Shardow.” Though far advanced in age, he was no laggard. In the one year I worked with him, there was not a single hard copy. Everything was electronic. He read meticulously, flagging every detail. We met only twice in person, yet by the time I finished, I understood what research really is. I once submitted what I called a concept note. He looked at it and asked, “What you sent me is incestuous. Do you know what incest is?” It was his sharp way of telling me I was citing only scholars from within the Department. “Look beyond,” he said. Even after the thesis, he kept checking: “How is our work? Has the work been passed?” He refereed for me, shared PhD opportunities in the UK, and agreed to supervise my PhD in the Department. Then, as fate would have it, he fell sick. We have lost a teacher, a builder, and a conscience. But the department he helped build, and the students he mentored, remain. – Authored by Dr Mohammed Shardow, a political scientist and a former student of the Department of Political Science, University of Ghana.

items.title: France : des dizaines de milliers de lycéens dans la rue
items.description: Plusieurs dizaines de milliers de lycéens sont descendus dans la rue mardi à Paris et en région, rejoints par des profs, des étudiants et des syndicalistes, pour continuer à réclamer des moyens pour l'éducation après plusieurs jours de tensions et de heurts avec les forces de l'ordre. Les défilés, où de nombreux slogans dénonçant la répression policière, se déroulaient sous haute surveillance des autorités, qui ne parviennent pas à répondre à la colère. Les lycéens dénoncent l'insalubrité des bâtiments, des classes surchargées, ou des absences de professeurs non remplacés, particulièrement dans les quartiers populaires. « La Gen Z se lève et veut être entendue » , dit à l'AFP Lilia, étudiante de 19 ans, venue manifester à Paris pour son petit frère et ses cousins. La jeune femme espère que la jeunesse sera écoutée par le président Macron, « au lieu de financer des guerres, il devrait financer son propre pays ». Après une manifestation dans le calme, des heurts ont éclaté à la fin du défilé parisien entre participants et forces de l'ordre, avec des jets de projectiles, gaz lacrymogène, grenades et mortiers d'artifice, ont constaté des journalistes de l'AFP. « Ecole négligée, jeunesse sacrifiée » , pouvait-on lire sur une banderole accrochée sur la statue de la place de la République, lieu emblématique de Paris d'où s'était lancé le cortège. Quelque 256.000 manifestants ont été recensés mardi en France, dont 56.000 à Paris, selon le ministère de l'Intérieur. Les organisateurs ont eux annoncé 450.000 participants dans toute la France, dont 100;000 à Paris. Cours suspendus Cette nouvelle journée de manifestation a lieu après deux semaines de mobilisation, émaillées d'incidents avec plusieurs lycéens gravement blessés, et dans un contexte social tendu à un peu plus de six mois de la présidentielle sur fond de hausse des prix et de recherches de coupes budgétaires dont certaines concernent les jeunes, comme les aides au logement. Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a condamné mardi devant l'Assemblée nationale les violences en marge des manifestations, réfuté toute « répression policière » et annoncé une suspension des cours en fin de semaine dans les lycées pour organiser un « temps de démocratie interne ». Il a également accusé la gauche radicale d'avoir le « projet politique » de « bordéliser le pays » avant l'élection présidentielle d'avril-mai et de « semer le chaos ». Au total, un quart des lycées (891 sur 3.700) ont vu leur cours « suspendus, soit totalement, soit partiellement » mardi, selon le ministère de l'Éducation. « Aujourd'hui je manifeste parce que j'ai peur pour mon avenir, et j'ai envie de revendiquer mes droits », a expliqué à l'AFP Selma, 15 ans, dans le cortège qui a défilé à Marseille (sud-est). A Toulouse (sud-ouest), Anne, 68 ans psychologue à la retraite, est venue manifester par solidarité. « Leur mouvement me semble totalement légitime et tellement mal entendu, en tout cas pour le moment par le gouvernement » , estime-t-elle. 215 élèves blessés Depuis le début du mouvement le 17 septembre, 215 élèves ont été blessés, « l'immense majorité » l'ayant été « soit dans le cadre d'accidents », « soit par le fait d'autres individus extérieurs » , selon les services du Premier ministre. À Tours (centre) la semaine dernière, un lycéen de 16 ans a perdu l'usage d'un œil lors d'un blocage, et lundi un adolescent de 15 ans a eu la main arrachée par une grenade de la police à Lens (nord). Onze enquêtes de la police des polices ont été ouvertes jusqu'ici. Le ministre de l'Intérieur Laurent Nuñez a assuré mardi que les interventions des forces de l'ordre s'effectuaient dans « la plus grande proportionnalité ». La Commission nationale consultative des droits de l'homme (CNCDH), organe chargé de conseiller le gouvernement, a exprimé mardi sa « vive inquiétude » sur les « recours disproportionnés à la force » et appelé le gouvernement « à renforcer le dialogue avec la jeunesse » et à « garantir l'exercice de leurs droits ». Plus de 700 blessés ont par ailleurs été recensés dans les rangs des forces de l'ordre et près d'une centaine chez les personnels de l'éducation. Entre rétablissement de l'ordre public et écoute des revendications d'un mouvement sans porte-parole très identifié, le gouvernement marche sur un fil pour gérer l'une des crises les plus délicates auxquelles il a été confronté depuis la nomination il y a un an du Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu. Les autorités craignent désormais un embrasement au niveau national, alors que les lycéens ont reçu mardi le renfort des étudiants. Lundi, l'Union étudiante recensait 32 sites universitaires bloqués. Les présidents d'universités ont appelé mardi à « des états généraux de la jeunesse » , estimant qu'il est « urgent de reconnaître les jeunes » comme des « acteurs » du débat public. items.title: I’ve been in therapy since COVID – Chris Rock
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye American ace comedian, actor and filmmaker, Chris Rock, has revealed that he has spent the post-COVID-19 years undergoing intensive therapy to confront personal insecurities and reevaluate the direction of his life. The 61-year-old entertainment icon made this known during a recent interview with The New York Times, where he opened up on his mental health journey, his emotional evolution, and why it took him over a decade to return to the director’s chair. According to Rock, the lockdown forced him into deep introspection, making him realise the necessity of mental healthcare and finding peace with self-worth. “I’ve been doing a lot of therapy the last few years, post-Covid, and a lot of it is about not feeling insecure. A lot of it is about ‘you’re enough,’” he stated. When asked about whether he feels insecure about his fame or industry standing, the veteran stand-up star dismissed the notion of status anxiety. However, he admitted that self-doubt occasionally creeps in when he observes his peers’ relentless work ethic or compares himself with other parents. “I don’t ever really feel insecure about my ‘status,’ per se. Occasionally I’ll meet people that are obviously working harder than me and that’ll make me feel insecure. Adam Sandler, Rick Rubin. You’re like, ‘How many things are you doing right now?’ And some people are better with their kids than me. I think I’m a good dad,” Rock said. Rock, who shares two daughters, Lola and Zahra, with his ex-wife Malaak Compton-Rock, noted that fatherhood and therapy have combined to reshape how he relates to people. He disclosed that a diagnosis of NVLD (nonverbal learning disorder) required dedicated professional sessions to unlearn certain personal habits that once hindered his private life. “The effects are that I’m really bad at reading nonverbal signals. I catastrophize, I have black-and-white thinking — both things that are great for being a comedian but bad in personal life and real relationships. So I’ve been learning. I have to see a woman once a week,” he explained. He credited the continuous therapeutic journey with fostering deeper emotional intelligence: “Part of all this therapy is developing empathy and really being able to get inside of another character. So the last four or five years, I’m a way more empathetic person.” Touching on his 12-year hiatus from directing feature films following his 2014 critical hit, Top Five, Rock disclosed that the gap was driven by a complex mix of marital divorce, financial obligations, and professional dead-ends. “Life, Covid, I got divorced, which meant I had to make real money. Maybe I had some other scripts that the market didn’t respond to. It’s not like I was sitting around. But Covid was a time to be like, OK, what am I doing with my life? And other [expletive] I don’t feel like talking about. I had a lot of stuff going on the last 12 years,” he noted. Rock emphasised that the self-examination helped him realize his true creative calling: “I should be directing small movies, character-driven pieces. Maybe I’m not in the movie as much as I used to be. So I’ve been writing a lot more.” That artistic realisation birthed his upcoming Hollywood drama, Misty Green, produced by A24 and scheduled to premiere on October 9. Rock wrote, directed, and co-starred in the feature alongside British-Nigerian actress Rosalind Eleazar. The post I’ve been in therapy since COVID – Chris Rock appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: BoG orders banks to give fraud units direct access to CEOs
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has directed banks to strengthen the independence and effectiveness of their fraud management functions, including giving fraud units direct and unrestricted access to managing directors and chief executive officers. Governor Dr Johnson Asiama said the central bank has received concerns from the Ghana Association of Banks about the different ways banks currently position their fraud functions. Speaking at a meeting with the heads of banks, Dr Asiama described fraud as a significant risk requiring serious attention from the banking sector. He said banks must strengthen fraud risk management through effective policies and controls designed to prevent, detect and deter fraudulent activities. “The fraud function should be appropriately positioned with direct and unrestricted access to the managing director or chief executive officer,” Dr Asiama said. According to him, the arrangement is necessary to ensure the independence and effectiveness of fraud management functions within banks. He also directed banks to ensure that personnel responsible for fraud management have the requisite skills, professional certifications and technical competence. The directive comes as the central bank continues to intensify its supervisory focus on risks emerging from the growing digitalisation of financial services. Dr Asiama said the BoG is also paying increased attention to cyber technology and fintech-related risks, noting that while digitalisation has delivered significant benefits to the financial sector, it has also increased operational and cyber risks. The central bank is therefore working with industry on implementation of the Cyber and Information Security Directive and will strengthen supervisory expectations around technology, customer-fund safeguarding and third-party risks.

items.title: Le Faso Digital 2026 : L'ARCEP renouvelle son engagement et parraine le Prix de l'Innovation inclusive
items.description: Partenaire de la première édition, l'Autorité de régulation des communications électroniques et des postes (ARCEP) renouvelle son engagement aux côtés de Le Faso Digital pour sa deuxième édition, prévue du 17 au 24 octobre 2026. L'institution apportera son soutien à l'organisation de la Foire, participera à son programme de conférences et de panels et parrainera le « Prix ARCEP de l'Innovation inclusive ». Un partenariat qui place l'accès aux services numériques, la qualité des services, la protection des utilisateurs et l'inclusion au cœur de la construction d'un Burkina digital pour tous. À quelques jours de l'ouverture de Le Faso Digital 2026, l'Autorité de régulation des communications électroniques et des postes (ARCEP) confirme son soutien à la deuxième édition de la Foire virtuelle des solutions digitales initiée par Lefaso.net. L'engagement s'inscrit dans la continuité. L'ARCEP avait déjà accompagné la première édition de Le Faso Digital, organisée en octobre 2025. Pour cette deuxième édition, qui se déroulera du 17 au 24 octobre 2026 sous le thème « Inclusion, souveraineté, innovation : Vers un Burkina digital pour tous », l'ARCEP a décidé de renouveler et de renforcer son accompagnement ; confirmant son rôle déterminant dans la construction d'un écosystème digital performant et inclusif. Un soutien renouvelé à Le Faso Digital L'engagement de l'ARCEP à accompagner l'organisation de Le Faso Digital 2026, traduit la convergence entre les objectifs de la Foire et plusieurs enjeux relevant directement du champ d'intervention du régulateur. Le Faso Digital 2026 entend en effet mettre en discussion des problématiques telles que l'accès universel aux services numériques, la réduction de la fracture numérique, le développement des infrastructures de communications électroniques, la qualité des services, la protection des consommateurs, la cybersécurité, la confiance numérique et les nouveaux défis de la régulation. Autant de questions qui deviennent déterminantes à mesure que le numérique prend une place croissante dans la vie quotidienne des citoyens, dans le fonctionnement des entreprises et dans la fourniture des services publics. L'ARCEP au cœur des débats de Le Faso Digital Le partenariat ne se limitera pas au soutien apporté à l'organisation de la Foire. L'ARCEP va également animer une conférence et un panel prévus dans le programme de Le Faso Digital 2026. L'institution contribuera notamment aux échanges sur les enjeux liés à la régulation des communications électroniques, à la protection des utilisateurs, à la qualité des services et à la confiance numérique. Cette participation donnera l'occasion d'aborder une question centrale : comment accompagner l'accélération de la transformation numérique tout en veillant à ce qu'elle bénéficie effectivement aux utilisateurs ? Car derrière le développement des services digitaux se posent des questions très concrètes : l'accès aux réseaux, leur disponibilité, la qualité des connexions, les droits des consommateurs, la sécurité des usages ou encore la capacité de la régulation à évoluer face aux transformations technologiques. Le « Prix ARCEP de l'Innovation inclusive » pour récompenser une solution à impact L'un des temps forts de ce partenariat sera la participation de l'ARCEP au Concours national d'innovation digitale 2026. L'Autorité a accepté de parrainer le : « Prix ARCEP de l'Innovation inclusive ». Ce prix distinguera une innovation capable de démontrer que le numérique peut contribuer concrètement à rapprocher les populations des services dont elles ont besoin. L'innovation est ainsi envisagée non pas uniquement sous l'angle de la performance technologique, mais aussi à travers sa capacité à résoudre un problème, améliorer un service et toucher des populations qui peuvent encore être éloignées des opportunités offertes par le numérique. Le prix fait directement écho au premier pilier de Le Faso Digital 2026 : l'Inclusion. Comment concevoir des technologies qui ne profitent pas uniquement aux populations déjà connectées ? Comment toucher davantage les zones rurales ? Comment prendre en compte les besoins des femmes, des jeunes et des personnes vivant avec un handicap ? Comment rendre les services numériques réellement accessibles ? Ces préoccupations figuraient précisément parmi les axes soumis à l'ARCEP dans la proposition de partenariat. ARCEP 208 solutions en compétition Le Prix ARCEP de l'Innovation inclusive intervient dans un contexte de forte mobilisation autour du Concours national d'innovation digitale. À la clôture des candidatures, le 30 septembre, 208 solutions avaient été enregistrées dans différents secteurs. Commerce et entrepreneuriat, éducation, santé, agriculture et élevage, souveraineté numérique et infrastructures, gouvernance et services publics, énergie et environnement, transport et mobilité, sécurité, finance et inclusion financière, culture : les projets proposés illustrent la diversité des domaines dans lesquels les innovateurs burkinabè cherchent aujourd'hui à apporter des réponses par le numérique. L'enjeu de la phase d'évaluation sera désormais d'identifier les solutions qui se distinguent par leur pertinence, leur caractère innovant, leur accessibilité et leur potentiel d'impact. À travers son prix, l'ARCEP portera une attention particulière à cette capacité de l'innovation à contribuer à un numérique qui ne laisse personne de côté. Un partenaire qui apporte aussi son expertise La participation de l'ARCEP illustre la conception du partenariat que Le Faso Digital souhaite promouvoir. Les sponsors et partenaires ne sont pas seulement invités à associer leur image à la Foire. Ils peuvent également apporter leur expertise, contribuer aux débats et soutenir directement les innovateurs. Dans le cas de l'ARCEP, ces trois dimensions se retrouvent : soutien à l'organisation, participation aux conférences et panels, et parrainage d'un prix du Concours national d'innovation digitale. Cette implication permettra également au grand public de mieux comprendre le rôle du régulateur dans un environnement numérique en pleine évolution. Car construire un Burkina digital pour tous suppose certes d'innover, mais aussi de disposer d'infrastructures accessibles, de services de qualité, d'utilisateurs protégés et d'un environnement dans lequel citoyens et entreprises peuvent avoir confiance. Réguler, inclure et encourager l'innovation Du 17 au 24 octobre 2026, Le Faso Digital veut créer un espace où institutions, entreprises, innovateurs, chercheurs, startups et citoyens pourront se rencontrer autour des enjeux de la transformation numérique. Le renouvellement de l'engagement de l'ARCEP traduit ainsi une conviction commune : la construction d'un Burkina digital pour tous nécessite à la fois de l'innovation, des infrastructures, une régulation adaptée, des services de qualité et la confiance des utilisateurs. À travers son soutien à la Foire, sa participation aux échanges et le parrainage du Prix ARCEP de l'Innovation inclusive, l'Autorité contribuera à mettre ces enjeux au cœur de cette deuxième édition. Rendez-vous du 17 au 24 octobre 2026, en ligne, pour découvrir les solutions, les acteurs et les réflexions qui participent à la construction du Burkina digital. Le Faso Digital 2026 « Inclusion, souveraineté, innovation : Vers un Burkina digital pour tous » 17–24 octobre 2026 — 100 % en ligne Le Burkina digital se construit avec vous. Une initiative de Lefaso.net.

items.title: PM Shehbaz says law took its course in AJK after 'unfortunate events' in recent months
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday expressed dismay over the “unfortunate events” in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) in recent months, adding that, however, the law took its course. He was addressing a ceremony in Islamabad in which four AJK Council members – nominated by the AJK Legislative Assembly – were administered the oath by PM Shehbaz, who is the chairman of the council. Referring to the “unfortunate events” in recent months in AJK, he said: “We all regretted it, wished that they did not do that. We all tried to make them understand with utter seriousness”. The premier did not name anyone specifically but was seemingly referring to protests by the now proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The government and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 refugee seats in the AJK Legislative Assembly, which resulted in violence-marred protests across the region. On June 5, the JAAC was declared a proscribed organisation by the regional government and placed under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA). A day later, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA. In his address, PM Shehbaz recalled that an all-parties conference was held in Muzaffarabad where “everyone spoke freely, though they were absent”. He said it was agreed during the meeting that after elections in the region, the new legislative assembly’s decision or the law passed by it, through consensus or majority, would be respected — an apparent reference to a decision on refugee seats. “But, unfortunately, they did not accept this noble suggestion. Nevertheless, the law took its course. […] Pakistan had to fulfil its political and legal obligations given that forces were working against Pakistan and the Kashmir cause on a foreign agenda,” the prime minister said. He also spoke about the four-day military conflict with India in May last year, saying that the Pakistani military, under the leadership of Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir, had played a “historical role” and taught the adversary “a lesson that it can never forget”. “I, once again, pay tribute to Pakistan’s armed forces and CDF Munir and congratulate them.” At the onset of his address, he congratulated the newly-elected members of the AJK Council. “This council is a bridge between Pakistan and AJK. It is my honour to have this opportunity to make this bridge stronger. “We will work harder for the progress of AJK and serve the people of AJK.” He also called on the AJK president and prime minister to fulfil their constitutional duties and resolve the public’s issues. “The federal government will mobilise resources to support your development efforts,” PM Shehbaz stated. The four council members sworn in today were former AJK Legislative Assembly speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar of the PPP from Muzaffarabad, former minister Mushtaq Ahmed Minhas of the PML-N from Bagh, former minister Chaudhry Muhammad Saeed of the PML-N from Mirpur, and Chaudhry Manzoor Ahmed of the PML-N from Muzaffarabad. They were declared elected unopposed as no other candidate entered the contest.

items.title: Mise à jour des données à la CBAO: une exigence qui asphyxie certains usagers…
items.description: Dans les rues animées de Dakar, la récente campagne de mise à jour des données bancaires de la Cbao (Grouge Attijari) continue de susciter des réactions contrastées. Certains clients disent avoir accompli la démarche sans difficulté, tandis que d’autres déplorent les contraintes liées au déplacement en agence et appellent à davantage de solutions numériques. Le soleil de l’après-midi plombe la poussière de Castors, mais l’activité, elle, ne faiblit pas. Au milieu du tintamarre des vendeurs ambulants et des coups de klaxon effrénés, quelques étals débordent d’une profusion de couleurs. C'est ici, entre deux imposants rouleaux de bazin chatoyant et de brodé suisse disposés sur son comptoir, que Ndèye Fatou règne sur son commerce de tissus. La quarantaine, le port altier et le geste précis, elle ajuste posément un voile en mousseline avant d'interrompre un pliage méticuleux. Dans l'allée, le sujet brûle encore les lèvres avec la récente vague d'actualisation des données clients exigée par la Cbao. Là où d’autres s'insurgent, la commerçante préfère s'en tenir aux faits. « La plupart d’entre nous avaient reçu ce message demandant de nous déplacer à la banque pour mettre à jour nos données », tranche-t-elle, le regard droit. Intriguée par la démarche, elle en avait immédiatement demandé la raison à son gestionnaire qui lui avait signifié qu’il s’agissait d’une obligation stricte. Elle n’a pas cherché à philosopher. « Je l’ai fait dès le lendemain. En revanche, les collègues que j’avais prévenus se sont entêtés. Aujourd'hui, leurs comptes sont bloqués », confie la commerçante. C'est un diagnostic sans appel que nuance aussitôt Awa, installée à quelques pas de là devant sa boutique de prêt-à-porter. Pour la jeune femme, la grille de lecture de sa voisine fait fi des réalités pragmatiques du secteur informel. « C’est facile à dire quand on a une agence à deux pas du marché », réplique-t-elle. Le Sms de la banque, Awa l'a reçu elle aussi. Mais, sur le carreau de Castors, le temps a un prix que le secteur bancaire semble parfois ignorer. Entre les clients à attirer, le stock à surveiller et la crainte constante du manque à gagner, la moindre absence peut être fatale. « Interrompre mon travail pour aller faire la queue équivaut à perdre mes clients », peste la commerçante. Pour elle, l'institution bancaire a manqué d'anticipation et d'agilité face à la réalité sociale de sa clientèle. « La banque aurait dû proposer une plateforme numérique simplifiée ou des horaires prolongés en soirée. Tout le monde n’a pas le luxe d'avoir la flexibilité nécessaire pour faire le pied de grue durant les heures de bureau », estime Awa. Un peu plus loin, à l'abri du soleil, sous l'ombre portée d'un immeuble, S. G. contemple ce ballet avec la sérénité des observateurs chevronnés. Ce septuagénaire, ancien cadre de l'enseignement, égrène posément son chapelet en balayant du regard les tensions du quartier. « Je suis fondamentalement contre ce blocage des comptes. C’est irrespectueux pour la clientèle », assène-t-il d'abord d'une voix grave et posée. Mais, l'ancien pédagogue ne verse pas dans l'indulgence aveugle et rappelle la chronologie exacte des faits : « Il faut être honnête ; cela fait quelque temps que des Sms d'avertissement étaient envoyés ». Pour ce témoin privilégié de la vie dakaroise, l'épisode met surtout en lumière un travers sociétal. Selon S. G., beaucoup de gens péroreraient sur les réseaux sociaux en jurant qu’ils ne se plieraient pas à la procédure. « Dans la vie, il faut apprendre à assumer la responsabilité de ses actes et en endurer les conséquences », conseille-t-il. L'analyse trouve un écho inattendu auprès d'Ibrahima. Adossé contre la peinture écaillée d'une boutique, ce jeune artisan observe la scène avec le recul de l'usager moderne. Pour lui, ce blocage est le symptôme d'un anachronisme bureaucratique. « À l’heure où l’État a audité le fichier national et où les données d’état civil sont numérisées, exiger une présence physique systématique est une absurdité », déplore-t-il. Pour lui, une application sécurisée ou un portal web auraient suffi plutôt que d'engorger inutilement les agences de la capitale. Malgré le dilemme entre la gestion du travail au quotidien et l'obligation d'aller faire la queue au guichet, la situation prend une tournure encore plus déroutante pour une autre catégorie d'usagers. En effet, l'assiduité et le respect des démarches n'ont pas toujours suffi à mettre certains clients à l'abri des désagréments. Certains usagers, convaincus d'avoir fait le nécessaire dans les temps pour se conformer aux exigences de l'établissement bancaire, ont eu la bien mauvaise surprise de découvrir que leurs comptes subissaient le même sort que ceux des retardataires. C'est le constat amer que dresse cet autre marchand du quartier pour qui l'application stricte des consignes s'est soldée par une véritable impasse professionnelle. « J'ai pourtant suivi les instructions à la lettre. Dès la première semaine après la réception du Sms, je me suis organisé pour me rendre directement en agence afin de procéder à la mise à jour complète de mon dossier et de mes pièces justificatives », explique ce client, la voix chargée d'incompréhension. La controverse dépasse la simple mise à jour réglementaire de la Cbao. Elle dessine en creux la fracture d'une société urbaine tiraillée entre la rigidité des institutions financières, la recherche d'agilité numérique et les impératifs de la vie informelle. D'un côté, ceux qui voient dans la règle un principe indiscutable, de l'autre, ceux pour qui le temps est une ressource trop rare pour être gaspillée dans une file d'attente. Pathé NIANG

items.title: Le F-16 le plus avancé destiné au Maroc a pris l'air
items.description: Le premier F-16 Block 72 destiné aux Forces armées royales a effectué avec succès son vol inaugural, selon Lockheed Martin. Le constructeur y voit une étape majeure avant la livraison du premier lot. Lockheed Martin a annoncé, ce mardi 6 octobre, le succès du premier vol d'essai du premier F-16 Block 72 destiné aux Forces armées royales. Ce vol marque une étape importante du programme d'essais en vol, qui prépare la livraison du premier lot d'appareils. Le géant américain de l'industrie de défense a fait part de cette réussite dans un communiqué. Selon le document, cet essai inaugural s'inscrit dans une campagne d'essais en vol menée en amont de la remise des premiers chasseurs à l'armée marocaine. Le constructeur décrit les F-16 Block 70/72 comme la version la plus récente et la plus évoluée de la famille F-16 Fighting Falcon. L'appareil se distingue par une avionique modernisée, des capteurs sophistiqués et des systèmes de mission améliorés. Il bénéficie en outre de caractéristiques destinées à renforcer sa sécurité et sa fiabilité. Mike Shoemaker, vice-président senior et directeur général de l'Integrated Fighter Group de Lockheed Martin, voit dans ce premier vol une avancée concrète du programme F-16 Block 72 propre au Maroc, ainsi qu'une phase déterminante pour consolider les capacités aériennes futures du Royaume. Pour lui, le F-16 demeure un maillon essentiel de la défense aérienne, aujourd'hui comme demain. Il s'est dit fier du rôle que l'avion continuera de jouer pour appuyer la souveraineté du Maroc et contribuer à la stabilité régionale pour les décennies à venir. Le communiqué rappelle par ailleurs que le partenariat entre Lockheed Martin et le Maroc remonte à plus de cinquante ans. Il a débuté en 1974 avec la livraison du premier avion de transport C-130 Hercules. Aujourd'hui, les Forces armées royales alignent des F-16, des C-130, des systèmes radar avancés et des hélicoptères Black Hawk. Elles doivent aussi être dotées, à l'avenir, des systèmes HIMARS, qui offrent des capacités de frappe de précision à longue portée. Sur le plan industriel, Lockheed Martin affirme son engagement en faveur du renforcement du tissu industriel marocain et des compétences techniques locales. L'entreprise cite en particulier son partenariat avec Maintenance Aéro Maroc. Dans ce cadre, un futur centre de maintenance, de réparation et de révision (MRO) doit voir le jour à Benslimane. Il s'étendra sur plus de 8 000 mètres carrés et sera conçu pour assurer la maintenance lourde ainsi que la modernisation des C-130 Hercules. Le projet ne s'arrête pas à cette seule plateforme. Il prévoit d'élargir ces activités à d'autres appareils, dont les F-16. Selon le communiqué, cet investissement soutient l'ambition du Maroc de devenir un pôle régional de maintenance, de réparation et de révision d'aéronefs. items.title: France : Marine Le Pen promet 140 milliards d’euros d’économies d’ici 2032
items.description: Le Rassemblement national (RN) a devoile le 6 octobre sa trajectoire budgetaire pour les annees 2027-2032. Presente par Marine Le Pen aux cotes du president du RN, Jordan Bardella, et du depute Jean-Philippe Tanguy, le projet vise notamment a reduire les depenses publiques et la dette francaise. Marine Le Pen promet 140 milliards d'euros nets d'economies d'ici 2032, par rapport au niveau de 2026. Elle affirme vouloir retablir l'equilibre primaire des comptes publics en 18 mois et ramener le deficit sous 3 % du produit interieur brut (PIB) en 2030. Le RN prevoit parallelement 30 milliards d'euros de baisses d'impots sur le quinquennat. Pour realiser ces economies, le parti propose, entre autres, une rationalisation de l'etat, la suppression de plus de 120 taxes, une diminution de certaines depenses liees aux associations et a l'aide publique au developpement, ainsi qu'une baisse de la contribution francaise au budget de l'Union europeenne, que Marine Le Pen souhaite plafonner a cinq milliards d'euros. Le RN inclut toutefois 16 milliards d'euros de depenses supplementaires, notamment pour revaloriser le conge de proche aidant, soutenir financierement les familles a partir du troisieme enfant et creer de nouvelles places de prison. Il propose aussi la gratuite du permis de conduire pour les jeunes disposant d'un casier judiciaire vierge. Sur les retraites, Marine Le Pen defend un retour de l'âge legal a 62 ans, voire 60 ans, et annonce une reforme instaurant un « pilier de capitalisation » individuel et collectif. Elle estime que cette reforme pourrait generer, a terme, entre 15 et 20 milliards d'euros d'economies. La candidate veut par ailleurs inscrire une « regle d'or budgetaire » dans la Constitution par referendum afin d'imposer une reduction annuelle de la dette. Le RN entend aussi renforcer la lutte contre la fraude a la taxe sur la valeur ajoutee (TVA) et reduire certaines depenses publiques. Sur le plan europeen, Marine Le Pen demande aussi une intervention de la Banque centrale europeenne afin d'alleger le poids des taux d'interet et de degager des marges de manœuvre pour les investissements. Jordan Bardella a enfin indique que le RN ne voterait pas « en l'etat » le projet de budget 2027 presente par le gouvernement du Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu, qu'il juge « mauvais, inefficace et injuste ».

items.title: LONAB: un plombier récolte plus de 83 millions FCFA
items.description: Le sourire d’Idrissa Kaboré en disait long. Ce plombier de profession, parieur depuis 1999, vient de décrocher un joli pactole de 83 371 500 FCFA au 4+1 du PMU’B. Ce mardi 6 octobre 2026, au siège de la Loterie nationale burkinabè (LONAB), à Ouagadougou, le gagnant a reçu officiellement son gros lot, avec en prime, un conseil: faire de cette manne financière un véritable levier pour son avenir et celui de sa famille. Il y a des jours ordinaires qui basculent soudainement dans l’exceptionnel. Pour Idrissa Kaboré, ce mardi 6 octobre 2026 restera certainement gravé dans les mémoires. Au siège de la Loterie nationale burkinabè (LONAB), à Ouagadougou, le plombier a officiellement reçu un gain de 83 371 500 FCFA, remporté lors du tirage du 23 septembre dernier au 4+1 du Pari Mutuel Urbain Burkinabè (PMU’B). Idrissa Kaboré intègre officiellement le cercle des millionnaires de la LONAB Parieur depuis 1999, Idrissa Kaboré a accueilli son gain avec une joie non dissimulée. Le chèque lui a été remis par le directeur général de la LONAB, Ibrahim Ben Harouna Zarani, au cours d’une cérémonie qui a également été l’occasion de rappeler les principes qui encadrent les activités de la Nationale des jeux. Pour le premier responsable de la LONAB, cette remise de gain dépasse en effet le seul bonheur d’un gagnant. Elle participe aussi, selon lui, à la démonstration de la crédibilité des produits proposés par l’institution. Le directeur général de la LONAB, Ibrahim Ben Harouna Zarani, apposant sa signature sur le chèque «Cette cérémonie est certes celle d’un gagnant qui vient recevoir son gain, mais elle est aussi un moment important pour la LONAB, parce qu’elle traduit concrètement la crédibilité et la fiabilité de nos jeux. Derrière chaque gain, il y a l’engagement de notre institution à respecter ses obligations envers les parieurs. Nous sommes donc heureux de remettre aujourd’hui à Idrissa Kaboré ce qu’il a gagné et de partager avec lui ce moment de bonheur», a déclaré Ibrahim Ben Harouna Zarani. Transformer la chance en opportunité Mais décrocher plus de 83 millions de FCFA n’est qu’une première étape. Encore faut-il savoir préserver et valoriser cette importante somme. C’est tout le sens du message adressé par le premier responsable de la LONAB à l’heureux gagnant. Le directeur général de la LONAB, Ibrahim Ben Harouna Zarani «Nous souhaitons que ce gain puisse véritablement changer positivement la vie de notre gagnant et de sa famille. Nous l’invitons donc à en faire une utilisation responsable et optimale, en privilégiant notamment des investissements susceptibles de lui assurer des revenus durables. C’est aussi cela l’esprit de notre slogan: Des lots aux gagnants, les bénéfices au Faso. Et nous rappelons à l’ensemble de la population que la LONAB demeure avant tout un jeu de divertissement responsable, auquel chacun doit participer avec mesure», a affirmé Ibrahim Ben Harouna Zarani. Un conseil qui trouve un écho particulier chez Gwladys Yaméogo, directrice du Pôle exploitation de la LONAB. Pour elle, la meilleure manière de prolonger la magie d’un gain consiste à lui donner une orientation utile. «Un gain de cette importance est une véritable opportunité, mais il doit être géré avec beaucoup de discernement. Nous encourageons Idrissa Kaboré à investir utilement, à renforcer son activité professionnelle et à diversifier ses investissements. L’objectif est de faire en sorte que cette somme puisse produire des effets durables, plutôt que de disparaître dans des dépenses immédiates», a-t-elle souligné. La directrice du Pôle exploitation de la LONAB, Gwladys Yaméogo La directrice du Pôle exploitation de la Nationale des jeux de hasard a également profité de la cérémonie pour annoncer les prochaines échéances de jeux proposées par la LONAB avec ses partenaires de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES). «Nous invitons également les populations à découvrir les prochains produits qui seront proposés par la LONAB et ses partenaires de l’AES, notamment le produit de pari sportif commun et la cagnotte, dont le démarrage est prévu le 12 octobre prochain. Il y aura également les rendez-vous de la Tranche commune Entente, les 7, 14, 21 et 28 octobre. Mais notre invitation s’accompagne toujours du même rappel: le jeu doit rester un divertissement et la participation doit se faire de manière responsable», a-t-elle rappelé. L'heureux gagnant, Idrissa Kaboré (1er à gauche) répondant aux questions des journalistes Le plombier a déjà son plan Pour Idrissa Kaboré, le plus difficile ne sera peut-être finalement pas de gagner, mais de bien gérer ce qu’il vient de gagner. Et sur ce point, le plombier semble déjà avoir une idée assez précise de la direction à prendre. Reconnaissant envers la LONAB qu’il remercie pour avoir été, selon lui, le canal par lequel plusieurs de ses rêves pourront se réaliser, il entend d’abord consolider ce qu’il sait faire: son métier de plombier. «Je remercie sincèrement la LONAB pour ce gain. C’est une grande joie pour moi et une opportunité qui va me permettre de réaliser plusieurs de mes projets. Je vais renforcer mon activité de plombier, investir également dans d’autres domaines porteurs et prendre soin de ma famille. Je veux utiliser cet argent de manière utile afin qu’il puisse réellement améliorer notre avenir», a confié le gagnant. Photo de famille Après 27 années de fidélité aux jeux de la LONAB, la chance a donc fini par sourire largement à Idrissa Kaboré. Mais derrière les 83 371 500 FCFA remportés au PMU’B, c’est désormais une autre partie qui commence, notamment celle de la gestion, de l’investissement et de la construction d’un avenir à la hauteur de cette inattendue fortune. Car si le hasard lui a offert les 83 millions, c’est désormais à Idrissa Kaboré de transformer ce coup de chance en réussite durable. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article LONAB: un plombier récolte plus de 83 millions FCFA est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
