items.title: White House denies Trump suggested Iran should ‘take out’ US cities
items.description: The White House pushed back Tuesday after Democrats accused President Donald Trump of suggesting Iran should “take out” the major US cities of Los Angeles and San Diego. Viral footage showed comments by Trump at a midterm elections rally in Nebraska on Monday, where he said high oil prices from the Iran war were justified by the need to stop Tehran getting nuclear weapons. “It’s a little bit high. It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe,” Trump said. “They can take out a city. Let them take, let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it’s going to be over with very soon.” Democrats — who control the state of California where both Los Angeles and San Diego are located — accused the 80-year-old Republican president of encouraging Iran to hit the two urban centers. “Donald Trump is now saying our foreign enemies should ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego. He is deranged and dangerous,” California Governor Gavin Newsom said on X. “The nuclear annihilation of an American city is no laughing matter,” Hakeem Jeffries, the Democratic minority leader in the US House of Representatives, said on X. But the White House insisted Trump was talking about the threat posed by Iran, branding it a “media freakout” that was “not rooted in reality.” “He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn’t been stopped,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said on X. The White House’s Rapid Response account on X took issue with a Los Angeles Times headline saying Trump had suggested “letting Iran ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego.” “No, he didn’t, you buffoons. He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance,” it said. Trump is hitting the road in the last month before the midterms amid Republican fears that voter anger over the Iran war and high prices could cost them control of Congress. items.title: «Excuses insuffisantes» : Séoul envisage des mesures fermes contre l'Ukraine
items.description: Les excuses de Kiev n'ont pas satisfait Seoul . Le ministre sud-coreen des Affaires etrangeres, Cho Hyun, a annonce le 6 octobre avoir recu des messages de son homologue ukrainien, Andriï Sybiha, apres la divulgation du transfert de deux prisonniers nord-coreens. « Il existe toutefois un ecart entre les resultats obtenus et ce que nous attendions, c'est pourquoi nous avons l'intention de prendre des mesures fermes », a declare Cho Hyun devant les deputes, rapporte Yonhap . Seoul pourrait notamment rappeler son ambassadeur en Ukraine. Le ministre a confirme que cette mesure etait envisagee, sans annoncer de decision. Une confidentialite demandee par Kiev, selon Seoul Les deux soldats sont arrives en Coree du Sud a la mi-septembre. Volodymyr Zelensky a ensuite annonce leur transfert devant l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies. Selon Cho Hyun, Kiev avait pourtant demande de garder l'operation secrete. Seoul souligne que cette discretion devait proteger les militaires et leurs familles. Le bureau de Zelensky a nie l'existence de cet accord. La presidence sud-coreenne a exige des explications et des excuses officielles le 27 septembre, avant la convocation du representant diplomatique ukrainien le lendemain. Le president sud-coreen Lee Jae-myung a reproche a Kiev de le faire passer pour un menteur en niant cet accord. Le 2 octobre, il s'en est egalement pris aux declarations du chef de cabinet de Zelensky, Kyrylo Boudanov. Celui-ci avait affirme que la Coree du Nord se preparait a combattre dans sa propre region. « Nous exprimons notre profond regret face aux agissements de l'Ukraine, qui semblent souhaiter le declenchement d'une guerre dans la peninsule coreenne », a reagi Lee Jae-myung. Andriï Sybiha avait evoque un malentendu diplomatique et souhaite un reglement rapide. Les echanges entre les deux ministres se sont poursuivis, sans clore le differend. Des soldats engages aux cotes de la Russie a Koursk Les deux hommes avaient ete captures a Koursk en janvier 2025. Des soldats nord-coreens participaient alors, avec l'armee russe, aux combats pour repousser les forces ukrainiennes hors de cette region. Moscou avait confirme leur engagement le 26 avril 2025 . Ce jour-la, le chef d'etat-major general des forces armees russes, Valeri Guerassimov, avait rendu compte de leur action au president Vladimir Poutine. Il avait notamment salue l'aide apportee par ces unites et leur courage face aux troupes ukrainiennes. Ce deploiement relevait du traite de partenariat strategique global conclu entre Moscou et Pyongyang, avait-il precise.

items.title: Germany arrests ex-spy chief on suspicion of giving secrets to foreign powers
items.description: A former German spy chief was arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of passing sensitive information to foreign powers, an embarrassing case that comes as the country is seeking to bolster its intelligence agencies. August Hanning, who ran Germany’s BND foreign intelligence agency from 1998 to 2005, is accused of espionage, treason and working for foreign intelligence services, federal prosecutors said. They did not say which foreign powers were involved. However, AFP understands that it was not Russia. Hanning’s former chief of staff, partially named as Manfred D, was also arrested on suspicion of aiding treason. The aide is accused of using his position working for some of Hanning’s successors to obtain classified information and sell to his former boss. Hanning then allegedly used the information in his private consulting work, which included preparing a briefing for a foreign spy and passing information to an agent of another foreign intelligence service, prosecutors said. Germany would “not tolerate the betrayal of secrets”, Marc Henrichmann, chairman of parliament’s intelligence oversight committee, said in a statement to AFP . “Whoever allies themselves with the enemies of our liberal democracy will be found out,” he said, adding that Hanning’s alleged behaviour would represent “trampling his official duties underfoot”. Treason can be punished with a maximum penalty of life in prison in Germany. The scandal is particularly embarrassing as it comes after the government last month signed off on a major overhaul of intelligence agencies, giving them broader powers to conduct covert operations. The BND and the BfV domestic spy service have traditionally had more limited powers than foreign counterparts, but authorities are seeking to strengthen them to face growing threats, especially from Russia. The reforms are expected to be passed by parliament early next year. The current head of the BND Martin Jaeger said that the agency had “quickly carried out extensive internal investigations” into Hanning case before federal prosecutors took over the probe. “For the BND and for me, there are no compromises when it comes to internal security,” Jaeger told the Rheinische Post newspaper, adding that the incident had “not called into question any of my aims or any of my priorities”. ‘Grave, deeply disturbing’ According to prosecutors, Manfred D. provided Hanning with approximately two thousand documents over several years, many of which contained classified information. Hanning — who served as the top civil servant in the interior ministry from 2005-2009 — used classified intelligence “to draft an analysis for an officer of a foreign intelligence service”, although it is not clear if “the material reached the intended recipient”. He is also accused of being “in close contact with a representative of another foreign intelligence service, to whom he passed on political information, partially based on material provided by Manfred D., for several years”. According to the ARD broadcaster, the information that Manfred D. passed on included material on the Iranian nuclear programme and the Russian army. It quoted security sources as saying some of the information came from partner intelligence agencies abroad. Konstantin von Notz, an opposition Greens party lawmaker, told AFP the allegations against Hanning were “grave and deeply disturbing”, and called for a investigation into the “potential damage”. The MP, who also sits on the intelligence committee, said he had repeatedly criticised the “dubious and wide-ranging lobbying activities of former senior civil servants”. “They are quite obviously also an entry point for hostile intelligence services,” he said. The allegations against Hanning came to light through his involvement in the case of Christina Block, a steakhouse chain heiress on trial for ordering the kidnapping of her two children. In that case Hanning and a retired police officer were accused of accepting a commission from Block of more than 100,000 euros ($112,000) in exchange for returning the children from Denmark, where they were living with Block’s ex-husband. As part of that investigation, Hanning’s property was searched in September 2025, leading to the current probe.

items.title: Human resource practitioners asked to embrace digital revolution for efficiency in service delivery
items.description: The Head of the Local Government Services, Professor Lord Mensah, has urged human resource practitioners within Ghana’s Local Government Service to embrace the digital revolution to enhance efficiency and improve service delivery. He warned that human resource managers who continue to rely on analogue methods of working risk being left behind as the public service increasingly adopts digital systems. Professor Lord Mensah was speaking at the 2nd Annual General Conference of the Human Resource Practitioners of Local Government Service–Ghana (HRPLGS-G), held in Kumasi. He said human resource practitioners must ensure that staff report to work on time, remain at post during official working hours and are productive enough to meet the expectations of leadership and the demands of the Service. “It is important for them not to be left behind because of the digital revolution we find ourselves in. If you continue to do things the analogue way, by the time you realise it, you may no longer be part of the Service because the Service would have moved far ahead,” he said. Professor Mensah also urged HR practitioners to ensure that information provided for decision-making is accurate and credible. He explained that inaccurate data could negatively affect decisions taken by management, particularly as the Public Service works towards introducing new digital systems. “As for computer programmes, when you feed them with wrong information, they will also give you wrong information, and that can affect decision-making,” he added. According to him, the Public Service is developing software that will require reliable data from Human Resource practitioners to support effective planning and decision-making. The conference brought together Human Resource managers from various Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies across the country to deliberate on challenges confronting the profession and ways of improving Human Resource management. The conference also featured the election of new executives for the Human Resource Practitioners of Local Government Service–Ghana. The President and Convener of the Association, Mr. Vivien Akumiah, also called on the government to invest more in capacity building and training for staff of the Local Government Service. He said inadequate funding continues to affect the ability of the Service to provide regular training and professional development opportunities for its personnel. “We lack training because we always lack funds to train. When we get support to build our capacities, I think it will go a long way to help Ghana,” she said. She noted that Human Resource practitioners operate across the country’s 276 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies and play a critical role in advancing Ghana’s decentralisation agenda.

items.title: PenCom advances pension administration with new reforms
items.description: The National Pension Commission (PenCom) says it is taking pension administration in Nigeria “extra mile” through reforms aimed at improving service delivery and expanding pension coverage. The Director-General of PenCom, Ms Omolola Oloworaran, said this at the 2026 Customer Service Week in Abuja on Tuesday. Oloworaran, represented by the Head of Surveillance Department, Mr Abdulrahman Saleem, said that the theme, “Extra Mile” reflected the commission’s commitment to service excellence. She said that the theme also resonated with PenCom’s vision of ensuring that every Nigerian worker enjoys a secure and dignified retirement. According to her, the commission has continued to pursue reforms aimed at building a transparent, sustainable and customer-focused pension system. She said the reforms were driven by the need to strengthen trust among contributors, retirees, pension operators, employers and other stakeholders. “Our duty is to ensure that we justify that trust through efficiency, transparency and responsiveness to those we serve,” she said. Oloworaran said that PenCom recently unveiled Pension 2.0, a new phase of pension administration driven by innovation, inclusion and integrity. She described Pension 2.0 as a bold step towards modernising and expanding the pension industry while improving the experience of pension customers. The director-general said that several landmark regulatory instruments had been introduced under the initiative to address emerging needs within the pension industry. She said that the guideline on the administration of Retirement Savings Accounts (RSAs) in foreign currency would enable Nigerians abroad to participate in the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) According to her, the guideline will make the pension system responsive to the realities of a global workforce and support the inclusion of Nigerians in the diaspora. Oloworaran also highlighted the guideline on the Personal Pension Plan (PPP), designed to bring self-employed persons and informal sector workers into the pension scheme. She said that the PPP would break longstanding barriers to financial inclusion and enable more Nigerians to build secure retirement futures. “PenCom had also developed the framework for the engagement of accredited pension agents to expand pension services nationwide. “The agents will play a key role in marketing and selling the PPP to underserved communities and individuals. “The commission had also issued revised guidelines for corporate governance for licensed pension fund operators,” she said. She said that the guidelines would reinforce accountability, transparency and ethical conduct across the pension industry. According to her, the measures were necessary for sustaining public trust and promoting service excellence within the pension sector. She said the recapitalisation requirement for pension fund operators would strengthen the financial resilience of the industry. Oloworaran said that the adequate capitalisation would help safeguard pension assets while promoting a stable, efficient and competitive pension industry. She said that the reforms demonstrated that PenCom’s mission was being translated into practical measures capable of improving pension administration. “Pension 2.0 is not merely about reform, it is about transforming the customer experience,” she said. Oloworaran said that the commission was committed to ensuring that contributors could access their RSAs seamlessly and promptly. She said that employers would also benefit from more straightforward and transparent compliance processes. “Effective service delivery remains the cornerstone of public trust, and PenCom is committed to strengthening its service culture. “The commission will promote open communication and enhance digital platforms through which contributors and retirees interact with the pension system, ” she said. She commended pension fund operators, employers, the media, government agencies and the public for their continued cooperation. Oloworaran said that collaboration, innovation and commitment were critical to delivering a sustainable and customer-focused pension system in Nigeria. The Acting National Coordinator/CEO, SERVICOM, Mrs Helen Lawal, urged pension agencies to prioritise exceptional service delivery. Lawal, represented by Sesugh Duruba, a Desk officer at Servicom, urged frontline staff to demonstrate empathy, professionalism, responsiveness, accountability and commitment in resolving customers’ complaints. She encouraged staff to anticipate customers’ needs, provide timely follow-ups and collaborate across departments to eliminate service-delivery bottlenecks. According to her, excellent customer service requires teamwork, innovation and continuous improvement, rather than individual efforts. Lawal said that the celebration should renew staff commitment to making extra effort a daily habit, rather than an annual event. She commended PenCom management for recognising frontline workers and promoting a culture of citizen-focused service delivery. She said that improved customer service would strengthen public trust and enhance the quality of service delivery across Nigeria’s public institutions. The National Chairman, Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Contributory Pension Scheme Sector (NUPCPS), Mr Sylva Nwaiwu, commended PenCom for improving customer service and pension administration. Nwaiwu said that the initiative had provided an avenue for retirees, contributors, pension fund administrators and other stakeholders to address complaints. He said that improved customer service was essential to rebuilding confidence and trust in Nigeria’s pension industry. According to him, the reforms have strengthened the CPS. He highlighted the payment of pension increase backlogs dating to 2007 and restoration of regular payment of accrued pension rights. Nwaiwu also cited the periodic pension enhancements, the PENCARE healthcare initiative and expansion of micro-pension coverage as notable achievements. He called for stronger collaboration between PenCom and pensioners to address other challenges confronting the scheme The post PenCom advances pension administration with new reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Élections au Québec : retour du PQ et percée de trois candidats d’origine marocaine
items.description: Les élections législatives dans la province canadienne du Québec, ont connu un bouleversement politique majeur marqué par le retour au pouvoir du Parti québécois (PQ), indépendantiste après 12 ans dans l’opposition. Trois candidats d'origine marocaine ont été élus. Les résultats du scrutin étaient pour le moins inattendus, surtout pour la Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) qui gouvernait la province et qui a subit une défaite spectaculaire, perdant tous ses sièges. L'ampleur de la défaite se mesure à la chute spectaculaire en nombre de sièges. La Coalition Avenir Québec est passée de 90 sièges à zéro, malgré 13,3 % des suffrages. Malgré ce score, le système majoritaire à un tour n'a pas permis d'obtenir de siège au parti. Même la première ministre sortante, Christine Fréchette, a perdu sa circonscription. De son côté, le Parti québécois, dirigé par Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, devra former un gouvernement minoritaire avec 59 sièges sur 127 alors que la majorité absolue est de 64, ce qui compliquera davantage sa gestion. Cette situation inédite ne s'était jamais produite dans la province. En effet, le Parti québécois a réussi avec seulement 28 % des voix. Autre fait marquant, les indépendantistes québécois sont minoritaires, ils ne représentent qu’environ 30 % de l’électorat total alors que près de 70 % des Québécois s’opposent à la séparation. La question de l'indépendance du Québec reste importante même si la victoire du PQ ne peut pas être interprétée comme une adhésion massive des Québécois au projet indépendantiste. Quant au référendum promis par le chef du Parti québécois « même sous un gouvernement minoritaire », il devrait être relégué aux oubliettes pendant un bon moment face au gouvernement minoritaire qui se profile, même si le sujet a été remis sur la table le soir même de l'annonce des résultats. De son côté, le Parti libéral, dirigé par Charles Milliard, consolide sa position de principale opposition officielle avec 40 sièges. Il occupera désormais une position centrale dans le nouvel équilibre politique québécois. Milliard a déclaré que son parti examinerait les propositions du PQ, et si elles « améliorent la vie des Québécois » et qu’il serait disposé à collaborer lorsque la réponse est positive. Au niveau de la communauté marocaine au Québec, les élections ont été positives puisque trois candidats d’origine marocaine sur huit engagés dans la course ont réussi à décrocher un siège à l’Assemblée nationale du Québec. Il s'agit notamment de Moncef Derraji qui a été réélu dans la circonscription de Nelligan avec un score remarquable de 63,25 % des voix , de Valérie Assouline qui a remporté la circonscription de Saint-Laurent avec 54,45 %, tandis que Nadia Boumftah a arraché le siège de Maurice-Richard avec seulement 307 voix d’avance sur sa concurrente, dans ce qui constitue la victoire la plus serrée et la plus spectaculaire de la soirée électorale. Ces trois élus font tous partie de l’opposition libérale, ce qui leur confère une représentation historique, mais sans pouvoir gouvernemental. Leur élection a donc une portée symbolique, toutefois leur capacité réelle à influencer les décisions reste modeste étant donné qu'ils se trouvent dans l'opposition. Leur rôle peut devenir particulièrement intéressant s'il arrivent à servir de relais sur plusieurs dossiers comme l'immigration et l'intégration, la reconnaissance des compétences des immigrés et la lutte contre les discriminations, l'éducation, l’emploi et l'entreprenariat, et aussi au niveau des relations économiques et institutionnelles entre le Québec et le Maroc. The post Élections au Québec : retour du PQ et percée de trois candidats d’origine marocaine appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Le Premier ministre : « la Mauritanie a très tôt pris conscience du lien entre le développement et le climat »
items.description: Le Premier ministre mauritanien, Mokhtar Ould Diay, a déclaré que son pays avait pris conscience très tôt « du lien entre développement et le climat, et avait inscrit la protection de l’environnement, l’action climatique et le développement durable parmi ses priorités nationales ». Le premier ministre qui s’exprimait ce mardi, lors de l’ouverture du Forum de haut niveau sur le climat, la paix et la sécurité (région du Sahel et du golfe de Guinée) à Nouakchott a ajouté que le gouvernement s’efforce « de traduire ces orientations en politiques et programmes concrets visant à renforcer la résilience de nos populations, à protéger nos ressources naturelles, à soutenir les secteurs productifs et à mobiliser les investissements nécessaires pour parvenir à une croissance durable et inclusive, créatrice de nouvelles opportunités au profit des citoyens ». Il a souligné que « le continent africain est particulièrement exposé aux conséquences du changement climatique, malgré sa faible responsabilité et encore limitée dans les émissions mondiales de gaz à effet de serre ». Cette situation impose, selon le Premier ministre, « de renforcer la solidarité internationale, notamment dans les domaines du financement climatique, de l’adaptation, du transfert de technologies et du renforcement des capacités ». » Il a souligné que ce forum se tient « à Nouakchott à un moment crucial pour l’agenda climatique international, alors que nous sommes à la veille de la 31e Conférence des Parties (COP31) à Antalya, en Turquie ». Il a souligné que « le renforcement du rapprochement et de la coopération entre les pays du Sahel et ceux du golfe de Guinée devient une nécessité stratégique » avant d’ajouter : « Nous devons donc renforcer le dialogue et la concertation, l’échange d’informations, les systèmes d’alerte précoce, la gestion intégrée et conjointe des ressources naturelles, ainsi que la mobilisation d’investissements en faveur de régions plus résilientes. »

items.title: UN chief hails Pakistan's 'pivotal role' in US-Iran conflict, calls for 'return to diplomacy'
items.description: United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres on Tuesday lauded Pakistan’s “pivotal role” in mediating between the United States and Iran as he called on the parties to end the conflict and return to diplomacy. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, he said: “Pakistan’s spirit of engagement is front and centre on issues of international peace and security. “I salute Pakistan’s leadership for helping to create the conditions for dialogue between the US and Iran and mediating that conflict. Your efforts helped deliver the Islamabad memorandum of understanding , the subsequent ceasefire and the framework for future negotiations . Every Pakistani should be proud of that pivotal role,” he said. “And from Islamabad, I want to send a loud and clear message to all parties: end the conflict, return to diplomacy and restore navigational rights in accordance with international law. There will never be peace in the region until the right of self-determination of the Palestinian people is recognised, as Pakistan has long championed,” he said. At the outset of his speech, the UN chief said that it was “wonderful to be back in Pakistan”. “I am in the closing months of my tenure as UN secretary general. Before that, I served ten years as UN high commissioner for refugees,” he said. “Pakistan has shown that, even in difficult circumstances, perhaps especially in difficult circumstances, compassion and responsibility must go hand-in-hand,” he said. He asserted that Pakistan mattered not only because of its size, but because it brought an “essential perspective” to global debates. “For decades, Pakistan opened its doors to millions of Afghans fleeing conflict and instability. Communities around this country shared whatever they had with people seeking protection and safety,” Guterres said. He added that the UN was committed to working together with the country to uphold protection principles and ensure that returns of Afghans “proceed in a voluntary, safe and dignified way”. According to the UN chief, Pakistan had put a spotlight on the value of multilateralism, dialogue, mediation and diplomacy at a time of growing division and mistrust around the world. “Those same values are vital within societies as well,” he stated. “Here and around the world, we know that inclusive institutions, respect for human rights, and a vibrant civic space are necessary to help strengthen social cohesion, build trust and enable people to contribute fully to their country’s future.” Guterres also appreciated Pakistan’s contributions to United Nations peacekeeping. “Pakistani women and men have served with courage and distinction in some of the most difficult and dangerous environments,” he said. “More than 180 brave Pakistani souls gave their lives in the service of peace. We honour their sacrifice.” The chief highlighted Pakistan’s leadership with Denmark on UN Security Council (UNSC) resolution 2823, which strengthened accountability for crimes against UN peacekeepers. One hundred and fifty-three countries co-sponsored the resolution, which according to Guterres, was the largest number of co-sponsors for a UNSC resolution in UN history. The UN chief also shared his plans to visit United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP) later in the day to pay tribute to the mission and to peacekeepers worldwide. Commenting on terrorism in the country, he said: “Pakistan has endured immense suffering. Thousands of people lost their lives. Families and communities across the country continue to bear scars. We stand with Pakistan in confronting this threat of terrorism.” He added that addressing terrorism and legitimate security concerns was necessary and indispensable. “Experience shows that the strongest and most effective security responses are those grounded in international law, human rights and the rule of law.” Towards the end of his speech, Guterres spoke about the climate crisis. “My last visit to Pakistan came during the catastrophic floods of 2022. I will never forget the utter devastation I saw,” he said, referring to the unprecedented floods four years ago that affected approximately 33 million people and claimed the lives of 1,700 people. “But I also saw the resilience, determination and solidarity of the Pakistani people,” Guterres said. “Pakistan is on the frontlines of climate chaos despite contributing only a tiny fraction of global emissions.” He appreciated Pakistan’s response to the crises, including establishment of the Loss and Damage Fund and the country’s growing clean energy transition. However, he asserted that leadership from vulnerable developing countries cannot substitute for responsibility from developed countries. “The G20 represents 80 per cent of global emissions. We need a drastic reduction in those emissions this decade,” he highlighted. “The principle of common but differentiated responsibilities must apply, but all countries must do their part,” he said. Meanwhile, Dar said he “greatly appreciated” Guterres’ visit, which he asserted was a reflection of the “long-standing and close cooperation” between Pakistan and the UN. “It also shows our common resolve to strengthen multilateralism and our cooperation at a time of profound global challenges,” he said. “We have consistently sought to uphold the purposes and principles of the UN charter, advance international peace and security, contribute to peacekeeping and strengthen multilateral solutions to global challenges.” Dar referred to Guterres as a “great friend” of Pakistan, adding that the country would not forget his solidarity during the 2022 floods as well as his efforts to mobilise international support for recovery and reconstruction. During its time as an elected member of the UNSC, Dar said Pakistan had tried to make “significant contributions” to international peace and security, with particular emphasis on dialogue, diplomacy, and the peaceful settlement of disputes. “Our initiative on resolution 2788 on strengthening multilateralism and mechanisms for the peaceful settlement of disputes is a reflection of Pakistan’s approach in this regard,” the minister recalled. “The unanimous adoption of that resolution reaffirmed the importance of negotiation, mediation, preventive diplomacy, and the good offices of the UN secretary general.” He appreciated Guterres’ engagement with the follow-up to the resolution, including the participation and presentation of “solid recommendations” in the open debate held in July this year. Dar said the country valued the secretary general’s “readiness” to extend his good offices in situations where dialogue and diplomacy could help reduce tensions and create space for peaceful solutions. “This is particularly relevant at a time when the international community is confronted with multiple conflicts and crises,” he reiterated. “Pakistan believes that the UN must remain at the centre of international efforts to address these challenges and that diplomacy must be given every opportunity to succeed.” Pakistan, Dar said, had played a “proactive and constructive” role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation in the Gulf region. He appreciated Guterres’ support for Pakistan’s mediation efforts and his recognition of the importance of diplomatic engagement. “Pakistan’s role in facilitating dialogue is consistent with our broader approach at the UN, which is to promote cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over conflict and peaceful settlement over the use of force,” he stated. The minister said Pakistan supported the chief’s UN80 initiative, which seeks to make the UN more “effective, efficient and fit for purpose”. “We believe that efforts to strengthen the organisation must reinforce its ability to deliver on its core mandates, while ensuring that the priorities and concerns of developing countries remain central.” According to him, stronger, effective, inclusive, and representative multilateralism was needed at a time of growing geopolitical tensions, conflicts, humanitarian crises, climate vulnerabilities and economic pressures. He further appreciated the UN chief’s “continued attention” to issues of particular importance to Pakistan, including regional peace and stability, counter-terrorism, climate vulnerability and development challenges. “We also greatly appreciate the UN’s consistent position on the Jammu and Kashmir dispute and the reiteration of the UN framework and UNSC resolutions for resolving the dispute,” he said. Dar said he briefed the UN chief on India’s unilateral move of holding the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance , which he referred to as a blatant violation of international law. “We underscored the need to ensure that India stops weaponising water and fulfils its obligations under the IWT.” He also highlighted Pakistan’s “deep concern” at the continued use of Afghan soil for carrying out terrorist attacks against Pakistan. He urged the UN chief and the international community to help address these challenges. Dar meets UN chief Earlier in the day, Dar held a one-on-one meeting with the UN chief, with the two discussing regional and global issues relating to peace and security, the Foreign Office (FO) said. The FO said the discussions covered Palestine, Jammu and Kashmir, Afghanistan, counter-terrorism and the future of multilateralism. Dar briefed the UN secretary general on Pakistan’s positions on Jammu and Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), reaffirming Islamabad’s call for a just and peaceful resolution of the Kashmir dispute in accordance with relevant UNSC resolutions. According to the FO, Dar also highlighted Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue and de-escalation, including its facilitation of the Islamabad talks between the US and Iran. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue and diplomacy as the most effective means of resolving disputes. The UN secretary general appreciated Pakistan’s longstanding contribution to the UN, as well as its diplomatic efforts to promote dialogue, mediation and de-escalation, the FO said. President confers Nishan-i-Imtiaz on UN chief President Asif Ali Zardari also conferred the Nishan-i-Imtiaz on Guterres in recognition of his “distinguished international service, leadership of the UN and contribution to global peace and development,” a handout by the President’s Secretariat said. The award, first to any UN secretary general by Pakistan, was conferred in a special investiture ceremony held at Aiwan-i-Sadr, the statement said. According to the handout the president also separately met with the UN chief and appreciated his principled leadership, his efforts for international peace, dialogue, diplomacy and peaceful settlement of disputes, as well as his constructive engagement with Pakistan and attention to the concerns of developing countries. “The president said Pakistan remains steadfast in its support for the Palestinian people and their right to self-determination,” it added. “He appreciated the [UN chief’s] consistent advocacy for Palestinian statehood and a two-state solution and said Pakistan would continue supporting efforts towards implementation of the relevant UNSC resolutions,” the handout detailed. The president further reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to peace and stability in South Asia, stressing that durable peace required sustained dialogue between Pakistan and India and the resolution of all outstanding disputes, particularly Jammu and Kashmir, as agreed under the UN resolutions respecting the sentiments of the Kashmiri people. He also conveyed Pakistan’s position that the IWT was a binding international agreement and could not be unilaterally suspended or placed in abeyance. President Zardari, per the handout, stressed that water should not be used as a weapon and an instrument of political pressure and that Pakistan’s water rights, recognised by international courts, under the treaty must be respected. On the subject of regional peace and diplomacy, Zardari said the country’s diplomatic efforts, including the Islamabad Talks, had been guided by the “imperative of de-escalation, dialogue and protection of human life”. “He reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to facilitate diplomacy wherever it could be helpful, stressing that there is no alternative to dialogue for addressing regional disputes,” the handout said. The president also spoke about counter-terrorism and Afghanistan. He said Pakistan remained a “committed partner” in the global fight against terrorism and has made enormous sacrifices in this cause. “Pakistan continues to face terrorism from groups operating from Afghan territory and has shared evidence concerning external support to terrorist proxies targeting Pakistan,” the president said, stressing that Afghan territory must not be used against Pakistan or any other country. UN chief’s visit Guterres arrived in Islamabad in the early hours of Tuesday for a two-day official visit. “Upon arrival, the secretary-general was received by Acting Foreign Secretary Ambassador Nabeel Munir,” the FO said in a post on X. The visit comes as Guterres’ 10-year tenure as UN chief is set to end on Dec 31. In its Monday statement, the FO said that during Guterres’ visit, Pakistan’s “efforts towards strengthening multilateralism and international peace and security, as well as its strides towards disaster preparedness and early warning, will be highlighted”. PM Shehbaz met Guterres on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York last month. The two discussed major regional and international developments, including the situation in the Middle East. In that meeting, Guterres commended Pakistan’s role and strong voice at the UN, as well as its contribution to international peace and security. The UN chief also appreciated Pakistan’s role and sacrifices in countering terrorism. Guterres’ first visit to Pakistan as the UN secretary general was in February 2020, about three years after he was elected to the position in 2016.

items.title: Développement local participatif : L’exécutif communal Golfe 6 renforce le dialogue avec les leaders religieux
items.description: Lomé, 5 oct. (ATOP) – L’exécutif communal du Golfe 6 a échangé, le vendredi 2 octobre, avec des responsables de différentes confessions religieuses sur leur implication dans la gestion participative des affaires de la commune et la recherche de solutions aux préoccupations des populations. Des prêtres catholiques et des responsables de la religion traditionnelle ont pris part à cette rencontre, qui s’inscrit dans la volonté de la municipalité de renforcer la concertation avec les différentes composantes de la société. Les échanges ont porté notamment sur le civisme, l’éducation, l’excellence scolaire, l’état civil, la salubrité et la cohésion sociale. La municipalité a souligné le rôle important des leaders religieux dans la sensibilisation des fidèles, en raison de leur proximité avec les familles, les jeunes et les différents groupes sociaux. Elle les a invités à promouvoir le civisme, le respect des règles de vie en société et la responsabilité citoyenne au sein de leurs communautés. 𝐌𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐮𝐫 𝐥’𝐞́𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐞𝐭 𝐥’𝐞𝐱𝐜𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐥𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐞 Temple vaudou(photo internet) Sur le plan éducatif, la commune entend mobiliser les responsables religieux autour de la promotion de la réussite scolaire. Ceux-ci sont appelés à encourager les parents à assurer un meilleur suivi de la scolarité de leurs enfants et à sensibiliser les jeunes sur l’importance de l’éducation. Le Golfe 6 prévoit également d’identifier, d’encourager et de récompenser les meilleurs élèves et établissements scolaires. Pour la municipalité, la promotion de l’excellence scolaire constitue un investissement dans le capital humain et un levier du développement futur de la commune. 𝐇𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐞 𝐚𝐮𝐱 𝐟𝐚𝐮𝐱 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐝𝐞 𝐧𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 La lutte contre les faux actes de naissance et les irrégularités dans les documents d’état civil a également été abordée. La municipalité a insisté sur l’importance des déclarations régulières de naissance et de l’obtention de documents authentiques, indispensables à la reconnaissance de l’identité et à l’accès aux droits. Les leaders religieux sont ainsi appelés à sensibiliser les parents et les fidèles sur les conséquences des actes frauduleux et à les orienter vers les procédures légales auprès des services compétents. Cette démarche vise notamment à protéger les enfants, dont l’accès à l’éducation, aux examens et à certains documents administratifs peut être compromis en cas d’irrégularité de l’état civil. Renforcer la paix et la cohésion sociale L’exécutif communal a, par ailleurs, invité les responsables religieux à renforcer les messages de paix, de tolérance, de respect mutuel et de vivre-ensemble. La réduction des nuisances sonores et le respect de la tranquillité publique ont également été évoqués afin de favoriser une cohabitation harmonieuse entre les différentes communautés. La série de consultations se poursuivra avec les leaders religieux musulmans, qui constituent la dernière composante de cette démarche. Elle devrait permettre à la municipalité de recueillir les préoccupations des différentes communautés et de renforcer leur participation au développement local. Vers un cadre permanent de dialogue Le maire du Golfe 6, Kokou Amenyenou, a annoncé qu’à l’issue des consultations avec les différentes couches sociales, la commune envisage de mettre en place un cadre permanent de dialogue avec les responsables religieux et les organisations locales. Ce mécanisme, a-t-il déclaré, devrait favoriser le partage régulier des préoccupations des populations, la coordination des actions de sensibilisation et la recherche de réponses collectives aux défis de la commune. La création d’un comité local de dialogue interreligieux et municipal figure également parmi les perspectives envisagées. Le 25 septembre dernier, l’exécutif communal du Golfe 6 avait déjà échangé avec des pasteurs de la commune sur les mêmes préoccupations. ATOP/KYA/AO

items.title: AMA intensifies enforcement to reclaim BRT bus shelters from traders
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has intensified enforcement activities to evict traders and other commercial operators from Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) shelters across the city as part of efforts to restore the facilities to their intended use and improve pedestrian and vehicular movement. The latest exercise, led by the Mayor of Accra, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, on Monday, 5 October 2026, targeted the Aayalolo BRT bus shelter near the former Telecel office at the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange, where traders had taken over portions of the facility, trading in mobile phones, accessories and other items. Despite the rainfall during the exercise, the Mayor, accompanied by the Coordinating and Finance Directors and the enforcement team, proceeded with the operation, removing tables and other items that had occupied the shelter and obstructed access for commuters. Addressing the traders, Mayor Allotey said the exercise was not targeted at individuals or intended to deprive anyone of a livelihood, but was necessary to restore order, protect commuters and ensure that public infrastructure served the purpose for which it was constructed. He said the rapid improvement in movement after the area had been cleared demonstrated the effect unauthorised trading activities had on traffic flow and access to the bus shelter. According to him, commuters who were supposed to use the designated bus stop had been forced onto the road because traders had occupied the shelter, creating risks for both pedestrians and motorists. The Mayor disclosed that a pedestrian had previously been knocked down by a vehicle in the area and said the Assembly could not ignore activities that exposed commuters to preventable danger. He stressed that the objective of the exercise was to make Accra functional again, explaining that restoring discipline in public spaces required cooperation from residents, traders, motorists and city authorities. “This is an Aayalolo bus stop. We have said in the media and at press conferences that people should desist from occupying the bus stops so that Aayalolo can work again,” he said. He noted that the public transport system was introduced to provide accessible transportation, particularly for vulnerable members of society, and said he would not sit by as Mayor while facilities meant for commuters were taken over for private commercial activities. He recounted instances where he had personally supported struggling traders with financial assistance, including a woman selling meat in Accra whose business had subsequently improved, to demonstrate that his administration was not opposed to legitimate trading activities. “We are all Ghanaians, and if Ghana must work, it depends on all of us. When we elect people to lead, we must also support them to succeed. Talk among yourselves, and let us do the right thing. Ghana loves you, and I love you too,” he said.

items.title: Afridi criticises Centre's counterterrorism policy as PTI's long march heads to Mattani from Kohat
items.description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi was leading a convoy from Kohat to Mattani, located on the outskirts of Peshawar, as the PTI resumed its protest march to demand the release of jailed party founder and ex-prime minister Imran Khan. PTI Information Deputy Secretary in KP Ikram Khatana told Dawn that the protesters would spend the night in Mattani. The march began on Sunday (Oct 4) from Lakki Marwat, and the Afridi-led convoy reached Kohat on Monday night. The protesters aim to reach Khairabad — which borders Punjab — by Oct 8, where the KP chief minister will announce the next plan of action. And while the plan for the trek beyond Khairabad is yet to be announced, the PTI — which is in the government in KP and in the opposition in the Centre — had previously announced Islamabad as its final destination. However, the Centre has warned the party against any protest or gatherings in Islamabad. But, PTI decided to embark on the march after weekend talks with the federal government to bridge their differences failed for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. Before setting out for Mattani, CM Afridi addressed the PTI supporters at University Chowk in Kohat and criticised the federal government over its counterterrorism policy. “Your failed policy did not end terrorism. Let me propose a policy under which peace can be established in 100 days,” he said, according to a statement released by his office. He said he was “not afraid of anyone and neither are the youth of KP”. “I have shared the draft of my demands on social media”, he continued, referring to a set of proposal he said he had sent to the opposition team negotiating with the government last week. CM Afridi said if any of his demands was unconstitutional or illegal, he would cancel the long march. The provincial chief executive rued that the PTI had employed all legal and constitutional means for the fulfillment of its demands, including meetings with Imran. But when one was not served justice, the Constitution allowed for peaceful protest, he added. He said the PTI would protest peacefully. He maintained that the people wanted a resolution of their issues through the provincial government’s policy, adding that there had been military operations in KP for the past 22 years but terrorism was still prevalent. “Your failed policy did not end terrorism. Let me propose a policy under which peace can be established in 100 days,” he remarked. He added that once they would decide to move to Islamabad, nobody would be able to stop them. Referring to the PTI postponing the launch of its march from Sept 27 to Oct 4, he said “they now have problem that this is Test match”. CM Afridi also said that there were reports that Imran’s health was again deteriorating in jail. He said if “Imran’s health is played with or he suffers any harm”, the jail administration, prime minister and other relevant authorities would be responsible. March will not be allowed to move beyond Attock: Kundi Earlier in the day, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi vowed that PTI’s long march would not be allowed to proceed beyond Attock in Punjab — which borders KP — saying the party “did not have the capacity” to do so. Kundi made the remarks while speaking to Geo News programme ‘Geo Pakistan’. “They cannot go any further than Attock,” Kundi said, challenging PTI to “try to take a step”. He contended that the party did not have “enough capacity” to march further. “They claim to have two million people with them […] show us the people; they don’t have the capacity.” Kundi said the province was suffering from terrorism and “yet, they [PTI] want to march to Islamabad instead”. Speaking about his recent meeting with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in Peshawar, the governor recalled that the two often held meetings to discuss the security situation, and during last week’s meeting, the two also discussed “dialogue with the PTI as well as the way forward in relation to PTI’s long march”. Kundi cautioned: “If there is a mishap during the long march — especially if someone from southern KP who wants to reach Islamabad to carry out a plot [is involved] — what screening mechanisms does PTI have in place to prevent that from happening?” He also assailed the PTI-led KP government for “staying silent” on terrorist incidents. “When the federal government asks for their support against militancy, they say that the army should leave the province and that we should hold a dialogue with Afghanistan,” Kundi said, accusing the incarcerated PTI founder of “having militants settled in KP in the past”. “He was called Taliban Khan,” Kundi added, referring to Imran. Kundi further claimed that KP Chief Minister Afridi was taking “directions from PTI leader Murad Saeed”, whom the governor described as a “runaway”. He vowed that Saeed “will be brought before the people and made to pay for his actions”. Speaking about the possibility of governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said: “If the president and prime minister hand the task to the province […] and deem governor’s rule necessary, the province will ensure its implementation.” He held that governor’s rule was the last resort. “Surgery is the last option; first, you are put on medication. No one wishes to do it,” he said, referring to governor’s rule. “We want to continue, but if you are pushed to the limit and there is no option left, then it is considered.” On Monday night, after reaching Kohat’s Lachi tehsil, CM Afridi said while addressing PTI supporters that this time, the party’s struggle was a long one that required endurance and sustained mobilisation, according to a statement issued by his office. “We must not exhaust ourselves. Our struggle is a long one,” he said, adding that, however, from Oct 8 onwards, a “T20 match” would begin. Separately, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also urged the PTI to end its long march and invited the opposition to sit with the government to resolve contentious issues through political dialogue. The march so far After launching the already-postponed march from Lakki Marwat on Sunday afternoon, the KP CM’s caravan reached Karak at night, where Afridi addressed supporters at Jail Chowk. Ahead of the march, movement on several roads in KP’s Dera Ismail Khan, Upper and Lower South Waziristan, Tank and Hangu was restricted under Section 144 for varying periods . On Sunday, former KP CM Ali Amin Gandapur, who was leading PTI workers from DI Khan to Lakki Marwat, took a U-turn from Yarik because of road blockades and the prevailing law and order situation. Noting that Section 144 had been imposed in the area for three days, Gandapur stressed that the party leadership had clearly directed workers not to damage public property or engage in any activity that could worsen the situation. Nevertheless, he contended that the return should not be viewed as a withdrawal from the protest movement, but as a temporary decision. In Karachi , a planned protest campaign in different areas was disrupted after police deployed personnel at several locations, blocked roads and detained several party workers and leaders. The PTI claimed that police detained more than 75 of its leaders and workers, including women, from different parts of Karachi. It further alleged that arrests made in other parts of Sindh, including Sukkur, put the total number of detained PTI workers across the province at more than 100. On Saturday night, an opposition delegation comprising PTI and Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), and a joint team of the government and PPP held hours-long negotiations , which ended in a deadlock.

items.title: Grande Promo Orange Money : Amidou Ganamé décroche le deuxième véhicule
items.description: Orange Money Burkina Faso a procédé, ce 30 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à la deuxième remise des lots de sa Grande Promo Orange Money 2026. L’initiative vise à renforcer la proximité avec les clients. Elle permet également de les remercier pour leur fidélité et de saluer leur engagement. Dans la matinée, plusieurs lauréats ont reçu leurs récompenses. La cérémonie a été marquée par la présence des premiers responsables d’Orange Money Burkina Faso. Les lots remis vont de 25 000 F CFA à une moto. Le premier prix a particulièrement retenu l’attention. Il s’agit d’un véhicule MG ONE, l’un des lots emblématiques de cette édition. L’heureux gagnant repart ainsi avec ce véhicule au terme de cette deuxième phase de remise des récompenses. Une initiative placée sous le signe de la fidélité Cette remise, pour le directeur général d’Orange Money Burkina Faso, Christophe Baziémo, de lots traduit la reconnaissance de l’entreprise envers ses clients. Il a salué la confiance accordée par les lauréats et invité davantage de personnes à rejoindre les utilisateurs du service. « Aujourd’hui, nous célébrons la confiance et la fidélité de nos clients. Il n’y a plus de raison de ne pas utiliser Orange Money. Le service fait désormais partie du quotidien. Il permet notamment d’effectuer des achats, de régler des factures d’électricité et d’eau, de payer dans les supermarchés, mais aussi de recevoir des paiements et des primes d’assurance » , a-t-il indiqué. Christophe Baziémo a également appelé les personnes qui hésitent encore à souscrire à Orange Money à franchir le pas. Selon lui, l’entreprise ne se limite pas à une démarche commerciale. Elle entend aussi accompagner ses clients et valoriser leur fidélité à travers différentes initiatives promotionnelles. Orange Money accessible à tous les opérateurs Le directeur général a, par ailleurs, rappelé que l’accès au service ne se limite plus aux abonnés du réseau Orange. « Vous n’avez plus besoin d’avoir uniquement un réseau Orange pour bénéficier d’Orange Money. Vous pouvez souscrire à Orange Money avec le numéro de n’importe quel opérateur téléphonique au Burkina Faso », a-t-il précisé. S’agissant de la Grande Promo Orange Money 2026, Christophe Baziémo a annoncé que d’autres initiatives pourraient voir le jour. « Nous sommes toujours engagés auprès de nos clients. Il y aura certainement d’autres éditions, peut-être pas dans le même format, mais nous continuerons à célébrer nos clients à travers les différentes possibilités de promotion et d’accompagnement », a-t-il assuré. Il a également exprimé sa satisfaction quant à la collaboration avec le partenaire Merveille Motors. Il a salué son accompagnement dans le cadre de cette édition et souhaité la poursuite de ce partenariat au bénéfice des clients. Amidou Ganamé repart avec le gros lot Pour cette deuxième remise, Amidou Ganamé s’est vu attribuer le gros lot de la Grande Promo Orange Money 2026. Il remporte ainsi une voiture MG ONE. Visiblement ému, le lauréat a expliqué qu’il avait d’abord eu du mal à croire à sa victoire. Il s’est rendu le lendemain dans une agence Orange Money pour s’assurer de l’authenticité de l’annonce. « C’est un cadeau que je n’ai jamais imaginé avoir un jour. Aujourd’hui, je suis très content d’être ici parmi vous », a-t-il déclaré, tout en exprimant sa gratitude à Orange Money. Amidou Ganamé a également invité la jeunesse burkinabè à participer aux initiatives de l’opérateur. « Je vous invite à prendre part à cet événement. Utilisez ces outils, soyez audacieux, car la science et la réussite peuvent frapper à votre porte à tout moment », a-t-il lancé. Après Yaginatou Ouédraogo, première gagnante du gros lot, récompensée le 3 septembre dernier, Amidou Ganamé devient le deuxième lauréat à repartir avec un véhicule. Cette remise vient ainsi clôturer la distribution des gros lots de la Grande Promo Orange Money 2026. Éléonore Savadogo Faso7 L’article Grande Promo Orange Money : Amidou Ganamé décroche le deuxième véhicule est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Lissô : le tournoi des vacanciers s’achève avec le sacre de N’Dantary
items.description: L’équipe de N’Dantary a remporté dimanche le tournoi des vacanciers organisé dans la sous-préfecture de Lissô, dans la préfecture de Boffa. La finale, disputée face à Touba, s’est déroulée en présence d’Ahmed Kanté, administrateur général d’AGB2A-GIC, dont le trophée portait le nom. N’Dantary a fait la différence avant la pause grâce à son capitaine Ousmane Bangoura. Ce dernier a été désigné meilleur buteur de la compétition. La finale a attiré plusieurs centaines de supporters ainsi que des responsables locaux et des représentants de la société AGB2A-GIC. La compétition était organisée par la mairie de Lissô en partenariat avec le district de football de Boffa. Le maire Alpha Issiaga Camara a indiqué que l’attribution du nom d’Ahmed Kanté au tournoi visait à reconnaître son implication dans les initiatives en faveur de la jeunesse et son rôle dans les perspectives d’emploi et d’investissement dans la zone. Les autorités communales ont également sollicité le soutien d’AGB2A-GIC pour pérenniser le tournoi, développer les infrastructures sociales et renforcer les actions en faveur de l’autonomisation des jeunes et des femmes. Ahmed Kanté a, pour sa part, insisté sur la nécessité de préserver la paix et la cohésion sociale. Il a annoncé la distribution prochaine de fournitures scolaires dans plus de 20 établissements de Boffa et de Tormelin, dans la préfecture de Fria. AGB2A-GIC a contribué à l’organisation du tournoi par un appui financier et la mise à disposition de maillots, du trophée et de récompenses individuelles. Pour les organisateurs, cette édition a permis de réunir les communautés autour du football et de renforcer les échanges entre les acteurs locaux, dans un contexte où le sport est présenté comme un outil de mobilisation de la jeunesse. Alphonse Bilivogui L’article Lissô : le tournoi des vacanciers s’achève avec le sacre de N’Dantary est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Napoléon Bonaparte était-il musulman ? La Grande mosquée de Paris s’exprime
items.description: C'est une question qui fait débat parmi les historiens depuis deux siècles : Napoléon Bonaparte a-t-il embrassé la religion musulmane ? Le débat est relancé à la suite d'une conférence de l’historien et ancien diplomate Louis Blin organisée mercredi 30 septembre par la Grande mosquée de Paris. Louis Blin : Il est “incontestable que Napoléon ait été musulman” L'historien a notamment affirmé qu’il est “incontestable que Napoléon ait été musulman”. Blin a consacré plusieurs livres aux liens entre l’Islam et certains personnages historiques français, dont Napoléon et l’islam, Lamartine passeur d’islam et Victor Hugo et l’islam. Napoléon, La Mecque, l’Arabie… Une page peu connue de l’histoire française. Invité des Mercredis du Savoir à la Grande Mosquée de Paris, l’historien et ancien diplomate Louis Blin revient sur les ambitions orientales de Bonaparte, ses tentatives d’alliance dans la péninsule… pic.twitter.com/AyLa2kUolH — Grande Mosquée de Paris (@mosqueedeparis) October 1, 2026 La Grande mosquée de Paris a dû clarifier les choses suite à cette déclaration. “Le propos appartient à Louis Blin, qui a consacré plusieurs livres à Napoléon, et dont nous ne doutons pas du sérieux”, écrit d’emblée la GMP dans un post sur son site officiel. La thèse avancée, explique la même source, est “étayée par des arguments (sources écrites et iconographiques)”. Napoléon musulman ? La Grande mosquée de Paris “n’a pas d’avis sur la question” Cette thèse ne nie pas “certaines ambivalences, reconnaissant volontiers le pragmatisme politique de Napoléon à ce sujet” et elle est “partagée par d’autres spécialistes, débattue, mais ne fait pas consensus et reste minoritaire parmi les historiens”, lit-on encore dans le texte de l’institution dirigée par Chems-Eddine Hafiz, qui assure qu’elle “n’a pas d’avis sur la question”. “La discussion scientifique sur les liens entre Napoléon et l’islam ne conduit pas à réviser notre passé. Elle permet en revanche de montrer, à travers un personnage essentiel et son époque, que l’histoire de France n’est pas étrangère à l’islam, à sa spiritualité, à ses cultures”, estimé la Grande mosquée de Paris, qui, par ailleurs fait l'éloge de ses cycles de conférences “Les Mercredis du Savoir. Initiés en 2020, ces cycles constituent “un lieu de débat ouvert, où s’expriment les avis les plus contradictoires”. “Nous sommes heureux de la qualité des invités que nous avons reçus et de la richesse des échanges que nous avons suscités, y compris sur des sujets difficiles”, se félicite la mosquée de Paris. L’article Napoléon Bonaparte était-il musulman ? La Grande mosquée de Paris s'exprime est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Lebatt ould Mayouf devant le juge d’instruction demain mercredi
items.description: Le président du parti « La Mauritanie en avant » a déclaré ce mardi que le juge d'instruction avait émis un mandat de sortie de prison à l'encontre du général à la retraite Labatt Ould Viah Ould Mayouf, membre du bureau exécutif du parti, afin qu'il comparaisse devant lui mercredi matin, 42 jours après son arrestation et son incarcération. Le président du parti a précisé que l’audience d’instruction était prévue à 10 heures du matin, ce qui constitue le premier développement de ce type depuis l’incarcération de Ould Al-Mayouf. Celui-ci avait été déféré devant le juge d’instruction et incarcéré en septembre, dans le cadre d’une affaire qui avait débuté par sa convocation à la Direction de la lutte contre la cybercriminalité, après la diffusion d’enregistrements audio qui lui étaient attribués et dans lesquels il critiquait le gouvernement. Le président du parti avait alors indiqué que le parquet avait retenu contre lui deux chefs d’accusation relatifs à l’atteinte à la sécurité publique et à la divulgation de secrets. Le parti « Mauritanie en avant » affirme que l’arrestation de l’un de ses dirigeants est motivée par des raisons politiques et avait déjà annoncé, à la suite de cette affaire, son retrait de la présidence du pôle de la coalition démocratique d’opposition et son boycott du dialogue politique prévu. Dans son communiqué, le président du parti a exigé la libération immédiate d’Ould Mayouf en plus d’excuses à son égard, à l’égard de sa famille et du parti, tout en réaffirmant l’attachement de celui-ci aux droits constitutionnels.

items.title: TGMA controversy hasn’t affected my relationship with Diana Hamilton – Piesie Esther
items.description: Ghanaian gospel musician Piesie Esther says the 2026 TGMA controversy has not affected her relationship with fellow gospel musician Diana Hamilton. Prior to the 2026 Telecel Ghana Music Awards, supporters of both Piesie Esther and Diana Hamilton were locked in a duel over which of them best deserved a slot in the Artiste of the Year category. The argument became more tense when Piesie did not make it to the biggest category but instead got her song Nyame Ye in the Most Popular Song and Gospel Song of the Year categories. Fans of Piesie argued that she had a bigger song and more significant optics than Diana Hamilton, and that the scheme had made a mistake by picking Diana over Piesie, who are both from the gospel side. Some radio and television personalities who rooted for Piesie Esther went hard on Diana Hamilton and suggested the organisers had been compromised in the nomination process. However, speaking to Doreen Avio and Kwame Dadzie on Daybreak Hitz on Hitz FM, Piesie said whatever happened had not affected her relationship with Diana Hamilton. “Not at all. That [a rift between Diana and me] will not be possible,” she said. When asked if she was disappointed that she did not get a nomination in the Artiste of the Year category, she remarked, “I was. I wouldn’t pretend.” “Sometimes I didn’t even want to go on social media because some of the things people said were frightening,” she noted. Piesie, who is out with a new song titled Great Change , is preparing for the fifth edition of her Flora By Grace concert, slated for 1st November in Accra and 15th November in Kumasi.

items.title: UEFA investigate Ireland-Israel tunnel bustup after spitting claim
items.description: UEFA confirmed on Tuesday that it has opened an investigation into the tunnel bust-up during last weekend’s Nations League game between the Republic of Ireland and Israel in Serbia. The row took place at half-time in the 1-1 draw in Backa Topola, with media reports saying that a member of the Republic of Ireland coaching staff claimed he had been spat at by an Israel player. Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later confirmed there had been a fracas. “Yeah, I was there,” he told journalists after the game. “I’m not going to comment on that one, that’s something that a disciplinary committee would probably look at.” On Tuesday, UEFA said that “following a review of the official reports which contained an allegation of an incident in or around the tunnel at halftime, a UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspector has been appointed to conduct the appropriate disciplinary investigation regarding potential misconducts from player(s).” Asked about the half-time incident, Israel head coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he “didn’t see anything”. It was the second time in a week that the two teams had played amid tensions over the war in Gaza. Ireland won the first match 3-0 in Hungary. On Sunday, Israel’s players wore black armbands to commemorate the victims of Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, after Irish players wore them to protest against the war in Gaza. The Irish players again bowed their heads during the Israeli anthem and the teams refused to shake hands before the match. AFP The post UEFA investigate Ireland-Israel tunnel bustup after spitting claim appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cliff Cheqona to take TP Masterclass to Lagos and Abuja in 2027
items.description: Identity and behavioural speaker, author and entrepreneur Cliff Cheqona plans to take his TP Masterclass to Nigeria in 2027, with events scheduled for Lagos and Abuja. The personal development platform, which has produced more than 81 episodes and held in-person events in Ghana and Dubai, is expanding its focus beyond trading education to personal transformation, leadership, emotional intelligence and purpose. Cheqona, author of You Are Not a Trader Yet , has been trading since 2012 and mentoring traders worldwide for more than six years. He said his work had increasingly focused on the individual behind financial decisions, rather than trading strategies alone. According to the platform, his experience with traders revealed that a sound strategy did not always prevent poor decision-making. Fear, discipline, emotional intelligence, self-perception and money psychology could all influence how traders responded to pressure and uncertainty. These observations prompted a broader approach that places personal development at the centre of the masterclass. “Once you start transforming the person, trading becomes too small a container,” Cheqona said. Cheqona describes TP Masterclass as part of a wider personal and spiritual mission to develop people and leaders. “God has given me a mandate: to transform minds and raise Kingdom-aligned leaders,” he said. The sessions now cover identity, belief systems, emotional intelligence, healing, faith, purpose, relationships, money, discipline and leadership. His philosophy centres on addressing internal limitations to achieve sustainable change in people’s personal and professional lives. Following its in-person events in Ghana and Dubai, the platform has identified Nigeria as its next major destination. It says the planned expansion in 2027 forms part of a broader African vision to encourage conversations about identity, psychology, emotional intelligence, personal responsibility and purpose. Although Cheqona’s Ghanaian identity remains an important part of the initiative, he sees its mission as extending beyond Ghana. The platform aims to encourage Africans to develop financially and professionally while strengthening their self-awareness, discipline, character and leadership. TP Masterclass describes itself as “Africa’s #1 Transformation Masterclass” and aims to bring together educators, entrepreneurs, psychologists, pastors, traders, creators and other thought leaders. Its stated focus now extends beyond trading, with Cheqona identifying the ultimate goal as influencing how people think, behave and lead. “Transform the mind. Transform the person. Raise the leader. Transform the generation,” he said. The planned events in Lagos and Abuja will mark the next stage of the platform’s efforts to bring its conversations on personal transformation to a wider African audience. TP Masterclass airs live every Saturday at 6 pm UK time on the Cliff Cheqona YouTube channel.

items.title: Bond market: Turnover rises 77% to GH¢2.76bn
items.description: The Secondary market activity strengthened, with turnover rising 77.13% week-on-week to GH¢2.76 billion last week. Trading remained concentrated in the 2027-2030 segment, which accounted for 70.08% of turnover at an average yield of 12.37%. The 2031-2034 segment contributed 25.83% at an average yield of 14.09%. The post-2035 maturities remained thin, accounting for 4.08% of turnover at an average yield of 14.79%. The September 2030 bond recorded limited activity, with turnover of GH¢1.12 millionn at a weighted-average yield of 11.75%. Databank Research expects the bond market activity to remain subdued as investors stay cautious ahead of the Wednesday, 7th October inflation print. The inflation data would provide fresh direction for treasury yields.

items.title: Shettima departs Abuja for Addis Ababa on high-stakes nutrition mission
items.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has departed Abuja for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, to lead a historic government-to-government peer exchange focused on accelerating nutrition delivery. The Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications, Mr Stanley Nkwocha, made this known in a statement on Tuesday. Nkwocha said Shettima would attend the forum on the invitation of the Deputy Prime Minister of Ethiopia, Temesgen Tiruneh, who is championing the country’s multi-sectoral approach to boost nutrition in the country. He said that the vice president would participate in the inaugural Nigeria-Ethiopia Nutrition Leadership Exchange Visit, a forum aimed at enabling key stakeholders to share experiences of building a federal, state and local compact on nutrition. Similarly, Nkwocha said during the visit, the Nigerian team would exchange experiences with Ethiopia on how a government-led plan can improve nutrition delivery. The presidential aide added that the delegation would tour key establishments dedicated to boosting nutrition delivery across the country. He said some of the locations scheduled to be visited include a wheat farm and a banana plantation in Oromia; the ‘Bounty of the Basket’ Training Centre and household visits in Mojo; and Jabdu Motors in Bishoftu. Nkwocha said that VP Shettima is being accompanied by Gov. Dauda Lawal of Zamfara, and Gov. Umar Namadi of Jigawa. He said also on the trip are the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Abubakar Bagudu; and Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Abubakar Kyari. He said the Director-General, National Emergency Management Agency, Zubaida Abubakar is also in the entourage of the vice president. Nkwocha said that the vice president would return to Abuja at the end of his engagements in Addis Ababa. (NAN) The post Shettima departs Abuja for Addis Ababa on high-stakes nutrition mission appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Be lovers of the environment – Archbishop Kwofie calls for stronger fight against environmental injustice
items.description: The Catholic Metropolitan Archbishop of Accra, Most Rev. John Bonaventure Kwofie, has urged members of the St Francis of Assisi Catholic Community at Tseaddo to actively defend the environment and oppose practices that destroy the country’s natural resources. He said the environmental destruction witnessed across Ghana, including the pollution of water bodies and degradation of arable land, poses serious risks to human life and should concern everyone, particularly those who identify with St Francis of Assisi. Archbishop Kwofie made the call during his homily when he paid a pastoral visit to the community, where he also confirmed 24 people into the Catholic faith. Reflecting on the life of St Francis, the Archbishop said the saint’s deep respect for creation should serve as a model for Christians at a time when Ghana continues to grapple with environmental degradation, including the effects of illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. “You know about Francis, his care for creation and his care for the environment. He loved the created order. Creation was our God’s masterpiece of art,” he said. Caption: The Community’s Chairperson Emmanuel Ani Acquah said the community’s eight-year journey had been sustained by the sacrifices of members, priests and its host family. He referred to St Francis’ Canticle of the Sun, in which the saint describes the earth as mother, the sun as brother and the moon as sister, to illustrate the spiritual connection between humanity and creation. According to Archbishop Kwofie, the destruction of the environment has consequences that extend beyond the loss of natural resources, particularly when polluted water and degraded farmlands affect what people consume and how they live. Caption: L-R (Parish Priest of St. Francis of Assisi, Rev. Fr. Col Francis Agyeman, Archbishop Bonaventure Kwofie and his Secretary Rev. Fr. Gerald Owusu Amankwatsea) “Our environment in this country is constantly under attack. Our water bodies are polluted, our arable lands are being destroyed, and we live under constant health risks from what we consume,” he said. Archbishop Kwofie further urged members of the St Francis community to see environmental protection as part of their Christian responsibility. “If you attend the Church of Saint Francis of Assisi, you want to be a lover of the environment. You stand against injustice done to the environment,” he told the congregation. He stressed that commitment to the Christian faith must also translate into action, urging the faithful to embrace generosity and support efforts that benefit their community. “Following Jesus is not easy. It is not a part-time job. To be His disciple is to follow Him wholly and entirely. It is demanding and requires total commitment,” he said. The Archbishop’s call comes as the St Francis community itself works to secure land for a permanent place of worship after years of relying on temporary structures. Caption: The Community’s Chairperson Emmanuel Ani Acquah said the community’s eight-year journey had been sustained by the sacrifices of members, priests and its host family. The community’s chairperson, Emmanuel Ani Acquah, told the Archbishop that its eight-year journey had been sustained by the sacrifices of members, priests and a host family that had provided support to the church. items.title: BoG declares FX compliance “non-negotiable” as it moves to tighten rules
items.description: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has issued a strong warning to banks over compliance with foreign exchange regulations, insisting that adherence to its FX requirements remains “non-negotiable.” Governor Dr Johnson Asiama said the central bank is consolidating various operational notices and guidelines issued under the Foreign Exchange Act into a comprehensive compendium. The move is expected to provide greater clarity on requirements governing foreign currency accounts, international transfers and trade payments. Speaking at a meeting with heads of banks, Dr Asiama said banks must maintain proper documentation and appropriate internal controls when conducting foreign exchange transactions. He further stressed that funds obtained or held for specific purposes must be used strictly for those stated purposes. “Let me emphasise that compliance with the bank’s FX requirements remains non-negotiable.” Dr Asiama repeated the warning, stressing that banks must ensure full compliance with the central bank’s foreign exchange requirements. The Bank of Ghana says the consolidated guidelines are intended to provide greater clarity for banks and strengthen compliance across the foreign exchange market.

items.title: Government to prioritise creation of decent jobs – Finance Minister
items.description: The Minister for Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, says the government’s New Economy agenda will prioritise the creation of decent jobs and the improvement of living standards for Ghanaian workers. He made the statement during a meeting with the leadership and members of the Trades Union Congress (TUC), where he outlined the government’s economic priorities. According to Dr Forson, the NDC government’s manifesto identified economic stabilisation as its initial priority, with a transition to broader economic transformation to follow. “If you look at the NDC manifesto, you will notice that we said we will spend half of our time to stabilise the economy, and after we lock in the economy and stabilise it, we move towards the microeconomy,” he said. He explained that the government had now reached the stage where it could focus more directly on the microeconomy, particularly job creation and support for businesses. “That is where we are going now, and so you will see us moving towards the microeconomy, where jobs, decent jobs are created,” the Finance Minister added. Dr Forson said the next phase of the government’s economic programme would place workers, businesses and employment at the centre of the country’s transformation agenda. The General Secretary of the TUC, Joshua Ansah, welcomed the New Economy initiative and expressed hope that it would create more opportunities and improve wages for Ghanaian workers.
