items.title: Blé : Le Maroc double sa prime forfaitaire à l'importation face à la hausse des cours mondiaux
items.description: Afin de préserver la stabilité des prix du pain et de garantir la sécurité alimentaire nationale, le gouvernement marocain, par l'intermédiaire de l'Office national interprofessionnel des céréales et des légumineuses (ONICL), a décidé de doubler le montant de la prime forfaitaire accordée à l'importation de blé tendre pour le mois d'octobre. Le montant de cette subvention à l'importation est ainsi porté de 20,80 dirhams à 44,48 dirhams par quintal importé, marquant une hausse substantielle de 114 %. Selon des sources informées consultées par Hespress , cette revalorisation exceptionnelle s'explique par les tensions accrues qui pèsent sur les marchés européens, en particulier le marché français. La poursuite des perturbations sur les approvisionnements en provenance de Russie et d'Ukraine, conjuguée au quasi-blocage du fret maritime en mer Noire, a fortement tendu l'offre mondiale. Cette situation a entraîné une flambée des cours internationaux du blé tendre, qui frôlent désormais le seuil de 320 dirhams le quintal, renforcée par l'appréciation de l'euro face au dirham. Face à cet encombrement conjoncturel, la revalorisation de la prime forfaitaire vise à combler l'écart entre le coût réel d'importation et le prix de livraison garanti aux minoteries industrielles du Royaume, fixe à 270 dirhams le quintal — un niveau de soutien qui n'avait plus été atteint depuis 2023. Les mêmes sources soulignent la complexité de la conjoncture, avertissant que la forte sollicitation du marché français pourrait conduire à l'épuisement de ses stocks exportables d'ici décembre ou janvier prochains. Si le blocage des exportations en provenance du bassin de la mer Noire, la Russie représentant à elle seule près de 30 % des exportations mondiales, venait à se prolonger, les mécanismes nationaux de soutien et de constitution des stocks stratégiques seraient soumis à une forte pression lors des mois à venir. The post Blé : Le Maroc double sa prime forfaitaire à l'importation face à la hausse des cours mondiaux appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: PM Shehbaz urges PTI to call off long march, resolve issues through dialogue
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday urged the PTI to end its long march to Islamabad and invited the opposition to sit with the government to resolve contentious issues through political dialogue. The opposition has gone ahead with its march despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad. The protest aims to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan. Addressing the groundbreaking ceremony of the Kashmir Chowk underpass in Islamabad on Tuesday, the premier said it was “unfortunate” that the “dreadful shadows” of long marches were hovering again, despite the PML-N and the PPP making efforts to engage the PTI in talks. The two parties, the prime minister said, held talks for two days in National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq’s chamber, and “it was hoped that politics of confrontation would end”. “Unfortunately, that did not happen. They [PTI] only had one purpose: to ensure that the talks do not succeed,” the premier said, adding that the opposition party demanded changes to things already settled upon. PM Shehbaz asserted that these protests and long marches affected the country’s economy and created hindrances in exports, imports and manufacturing. “We collectively improved the economy in 2.5 years and reached macroeconomic stability. Now is the time for it to flourish,” the premier added. “In September, our information technology exports, remittances and the country’s production improved,” he said. “If someone harms it, is it not equivalent to being an enemy of the country?” The premier stressed that putting the economy in shambles and the lives of people in danger will not be allowed. “The law will take its course,” he said. “I will still say: come to your senses. Will your actions harm the country or benefit it? … End your long march and protests. When you end them, we will surely sit down with you,” he said. Earlier in the same ceremony, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said, without naming anyone, that people had to see for themselves which public representatives were working for their welfare and which ones were engaging in “negative politics”. Responding to the premier’s remarks, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Khan said that talks remained “limited to offers”. “No positive step gets taken and it is a matter of great concern for us,” he said while speaking to reporters outside Adiala jail. He pointed out that it had been almost a year since the party’s last meeting with Imran on Oct 16, 2025, calling this “inhumane”. He also criticised that Imran was being denied meetings with his doctors, family, lawyers, and party, saying: “We did not want to sit for a photo session together with you.” Gohar added that the party had always stood with the state and put Pakistan first, yet they were still not granted access to their leader. Tallal says talks conditional on PTI calling off march Separately, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry also spoke about the resumption of talks, saying that it remained conditional upon PTI calling off its marches and protests. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he warned that constitutional and political measures were in place to respond to the PTI’s ongoing long march and held Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi responsible for the breakdown in negotiations. “Political and constitutional measures are in place,” Chaudhry said. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry speaks to media on Oct 6, 2026. — DawnNewsTV He added that the “wise” people part of the PTI’s delegation had tried to make the talks successful. Chaudhry further said that if the talks had succeeded, Pakistan would have had a united political front and the PTI would have gained “political space”. He added that a “hardening of the state” was now close, stressing that “enough softness has been shown”. “The state is like a mother, but it also has to act like a father at times,” Chaudhry said. “Constitutional options are under discussion, but the political option comes first,” he said. Commenting on the talks, Chaudhry told reporters that on the first day, Naqvi presented the government’s position regarding terrorism in KP, which included facts about the provincial government’s lack of involvement in the province’s affairs, budget and counterterrorism efforts. Chaudhry said the next day, the PTI delegation returned to Islamabad to continue talks after discussing the terms of the agreement with KP’s senior leadership in Peshawar. He said CM Afridi had previously reassured the Centre that the PTI delegation had the authority to reach an agreement on behalf of the provincial government. “We were assured that on terrorism, they [PTI] agreed 100 per cent on the federal government’s points,” Chaudhry said, adding that it was only then that Naqvi travelled to Lahore to PM Shehbaz and informed him that the PTI and the PML-N had agreed on the terrorism issue. “The prime minister said, ‘give as much political space as you can’,” Chaudhry told the media. According to him, PM Shehbaz told Naqvi that “parties’ political capital comes and goes”. Chaudhry said the premier further told Naqvi that when Pakistan was on the brink of financial default, strict measures reduced PML-N’s political capital, but they ensured that the country would not default. The second day of the talks started after the two sides had agreed on the issue of terrorism, Chaudhry said. “The win for us in the draft agreement was that we would be successful in bringing the PTI to the same page for eliminating terrorism,” he said. The draft was ready by 9pm on the second day of the talks, and Naqvi was getting ready to take it to President Asif Ali Zardari, according to the state minister. “Everything was fine,” he said, adding that some back and forth happened on further edits, but they were all agreed upon. “At the last minute, the opposition sat in a separate room for a while to consult with the KP chief minister. When they came out, they couldn’t look us in the eye and asked for permission to leave,” Chaudhry said. He added that the PTI delegation thanked the PML-N for patiently conducting the talks. The nation had agreed on the two National Action Plans (NAP) against terrorism, Chaudhry said, adding that the second plan was agreed upon during the PTI’s government under former prime minister Imran. He said that NAP was linked to “Pakistan’s Constitution, its needs, security, stability and Islamic teachings”. Citing Afridi’s statement that he wouldn’t allow a plan against the people of KP, Chaudhry questioned if Imran’s NAP was against the people of the province. Chaudhry claimed that KP was unsafe for common people and politicians alike; however, he noted that at the same time, the PTI’s leaders and workers were safe from threats in the same region. “The only one safe there is PTI,” he said, questioning, “Why do [terrorists] have a soft corner for you only?” On the possibility of talks resuming, Chaudhry said that any further talks were conditional upon the PTI calling off its marches and protests. “Don’t encourage terrorists. Instead, let’s kill them together,” Chaudhry further stated. Opp-govt dialogue failure Over the weekend, the government and opposition held two rounds of talks , which did not yield positive results, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points. On Sunday, the PTI said it wanted immediate access to party chief Imran for consultations, and even agreed to forgo other demands in return for a meeting with Imran. However, the government declined to make access to Imran part of the proposed agreement, the opposition party claimed. Another deadlock was terrorism in KP. The federal government asked the KP government to support its counterterrorism measures and support emergency measures within 72 hours in the merged tribal districts, the PTI said. Instead, the PTI proposed that authorised representatives of the federal and KP governments meet within 72 hours to develop a clear, comprehensive and mutually agreed strategy for peace and counterterrorism, the statement added. The PTI said the health and medical treatment of Imran Khan was also raised as a matter of fundamental importance. Meanwhile, PTI leader Salman Akram Raja, who was a part of the opposition’s delegation, said the primary reason for the failure was disagreement on anti-terrorism actions in KP. Raja said the opposition stood firm on its principled position that anti-terrorism actions should be based on an agreement between the federal government and the KP government, and would be framed in consultation with stakeholders. After talks between the government and the opposition ended without headway, interior minister Naqvi on Sunday accused CM Afridi of “sabotaging” negotiations. On Sunday, Naqvi also held a meeting with KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi to discuss the political and security situation amid speculations of ‘imminent’ governor’s rule in the province. A government source told Dawn that the government was seriously considering the imposition of the governor’s rule in KP. But Special Assistant to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Monday that a return to negotiations was possible if there was an assurance of positive progress by the opposition regarding counterterrorism efforts in KP. Speaking on Geo News ’ programme ‘Capital Talk’, he said that the federal government aimed to end terrorism in Pakistan, protect its borders and keep people safe. “The provincial government will have to play its role at any cost in this policy and operation,” he added. He said that both sides were still in contact, and said that if “better sense prevails” amongst the opposition and they could provide “assurance of some positive progress” in this regard, then they could sit down for more talks.

items.title: Ghana’s ocean is not land under water: Why the Fisheries Commission is right to demand a proper assessment of offshore gold exploration
items.description: INTRODUCTION AND CONTEXT: BEYOND A DISPUTE BETWEEN TWO NATIONAL INSTITUTIONS The Fisheries Commission’s objection to the reported grant of an offshore reconnaissance licence to Gold Coast GRC Ghana Ltd, covering approximately 10,000 square kilometres of Ghana’s shallow continental shelf, goes beyond a disagreement between two state institutions. It poses a fundamental question for Ghana’s ocean governance: Can a terrestrial mining regulatory template adequately govern a major extractive activity in the marine environment? The answer should be no. Ghana has sovereign rights to explore and exploit mineral resources within its maritime jurisdiction, but those rights coexist with obligations to protect fisheries, marine biodiversity, and the marine environment. The issue is therefore not whether Ghana may explore offshore mineral resources, but whether the regulatory process adequately reflects the environmental, scientific, and socioeconomic characteristics of the sea. The Fisheries Commission’s concerns are consequently material. A framework referring principally to terrestrial considerations cannot substitute for marine-specific information on bathymetry, seabed characteristics, oceanography, water quality, fisheries resources, benthic habitats, spawning and nursery grounds, underwater noise, vessel interactions, pollution risks, and fishing livelihoods. Ghana’s offshore petroleum experience is instructive. Owusu, Lawer, Adjei and Ogbe (2023), writing in Maritime Studies, document conflicts between offshore petroleum activities and small-scale fisheries, including competition over marine space and effects on coastal livelihoods. Adjei and Overå (2019) similarly demonstrate the institutional and livelihood tensions arising from coexistence between petroleum operations and small-scale fisheries. The offshore gold proposal should therefore be assessed against lessons Ghana has already learned from another offshore extractive industry. EEZ, CONTINENTAL SHELF, AND THE AREA: THE LEGAL GEOGRAPHY MATTERS Three maritime concepts are particularly relevant under this discussion: the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the continental shelf, and the Area. They are legally distinct. Under UNCLOS Articles 56 and 57, Ghana’s EEZ may extend up to 200 nautical miles from the applicable baselines. Within it, Ghana enjoys sovereign rights to explore, exploit, conserve, and manage living and non-living natural resources of the waters, seabed, and subsoil, together with jurisdiction over specified matters including marine scientific research and protection and preservation of the marine environment. The continental shelf concerns the seabed and subsoil, not the superjacent water column. Under UNCLOS Article 76, every coastal State possesses a continental shelf at least to 200 nautical miles where the continental margin does not extend that far. Where the geological conditions specified by Article 76 are satisfied, the continental shelf may extend beyond 200 nautical miles. Its outer limit is subject to detailed formulae and constraints. In relevant circumstances, one of the principal constraints is a 350-nautical-mile limit from the baselines, although UNCLOS also contains an alternative 100-nautical-mile limit measured from the 2,500-metre isobath and special rules concerning submarine ridges. It is therefore more accurate to say that a State’s continental shelf may, where UNCLOS Article 76 criteria are satisfied, extend beyond 200 nautical miles and, subject to the applicable rules, up to the 350-nautical-mile constraint. It is not correct to assume that every coastal State automatically possesses a 350-nautical-mile continental shelf. Ghana secured its 350nm continental shelf extension on September 5, 2014. For offshore gold, Article 77 is particularly important. It gives the coastal State exclusive sovereign rights to explore and exploit mineral and other non-living resources of the continental shelf. If Ghana does not exploit those resources, no other entity may do so without Ghana’s express consent. This makes the distinction between the EEZ and continental shelf important. Fish and other living resources in the water column primarily engage Ghana’s EEZ jurisdiction, whereas gold occurring in the seabed or subsoil engages Ghana’s continental-shelf rights. Beyond the limits of national jurisdiction over the seabed lies what UNCLOS formally calls “the Area.” Under Article 1(1) (1), the Area means the seabed and ocean floor and subsoil thereof beyond the limits of national jurisdiction. Under Article 136, the Area and its resources are the common heritage of mankind. No State may claim sovereignty or sovereign rights over any part of the Area or its resources: Article 137 expressly prohibits such appropriation. Mineral-resource activities in the Area consequently operate under the international regime established by UNCLOS Part XI and the International Seabed Authority rather than the exclusive resource jurisdiction of an individual coastal State. This distinction matters for environmental assessment because marine environmental effects do not necessarily stop where legal jurisdiction ends. GHANA’S NATIONAL LAW: THE FIRST LINE OF REGULATION The immediate regulatory analysis should begin with Ghanaian law. Mineral-resource jurisdiction does not exclude fisheries and environmental jurisdiction merely because the proposed activity is classified as mineral reconnaissance. Once the activity occurs at sea, several statutory mandates may be engaged simultaneously. Section 50 of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146) is particularly relevant. It addresses non-fishing activities likely to have a substantial impact on fisheries or other aquatic resources and provides for Fisheries Commission involvement and Fisheries Impact Assessment where the statutory threshold is met. Importantly, the fisheries assessment requirement operates in addition to applicable requirements of the Environmental Protection Authority. The consequence is significant: neither a mineral reconnaissance licence nor a general environmental authorisation necessarily exhausts the regulatory requirements applicable to an offshore activity. The Fisheries Commission, Minerals Commission and Environmental Protection Authority therefore exercise distinct but intersecting statutory mandates. Depending upon the nature of the operation, the Ghana Maritime Authority and other competent institutions may also have responsibilities concerning navigation, vessel operations, marine pollution and safety. The relevant regulatory question is not which institution “owns” the project, but which statutory mandates are triggered by its location, activities and potential effects. WHY THE FISHERIES COMMISSION’S INTERVENTION IS ESSENTIAL The Fisheries Commission’s involvement in the grant of the reconnaissance is both statutory and technical. Under section 50 of the Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146), non-fishing activities likely to substantially affect fisheries or aquatic resources require appropriate fisheries assessment. A credible marine baseline should therefore cover seabed conditions, oceanography, water quality, marine habitats, fish stocks, spawning and nursery grounds, fishing areas, vessel movements and fisheries-dependent livelihoods. Without this baseline, project-related impacts cannot reliably be distinguished from existing pressures from fishing, shipping, petroleum operations and other activities. The Commission’s scientific expertise and fisheries data are therefore essential for identifying direct and cumulative impacts and determining appropriate mitigation and monitoring measures. UNCLOS: RESOURCE RIGHTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL DUTIES UNCLOS does not separate resource development from environmental responsibility. Article 192 establishes the obligation to protect and preserve the marine environment, while Article 193 recognises the sovereign right to exploit natural resources subject to that environmental duty. Article 194 requires States to take measures to prevent, reduce and control pollution of the marine environment. These provisions apply alongside Ghana’s resource rights under Articles 56 and 77. Ghana’s sovereign right to exploit offshore resources does not displace its obligation to protect the marine environment; both obligations must be implemented together. ARTICLE 206: ASSESSMENT BEFORE ENVIRONMENTAL HARM UNCLOS Article 206 provides the principal EIA Bridge. Where a State has reasonable grounds to believe that planned activities under its jurisdiction or control may cause substantial pollution or significant and harmful changes to the marine environment, it must as far as practicable, assess their potential effects. The importance of this provision extends beyond the immediate project location. Ocean currents, sediment movement, pollution, underwater noise, migratory species and ecological processes do not necessarily conform to jurisdictional boundaries. Accordingly, an activity authorised within national jurisdiction may produce effects beyond it. This is why environmental assessment must consider not only where an activity occurs, but also where its effects may occur. The International Court of Justice’s decision in Pulp Mills on the River Uruguay (2010) reinforces the preventive role of EIA where activities present risks of significant adverse transboundary effects. The jurisprudence of the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea has likewise developed the due-diligence content of States’ obligations to protect the marine environment. FROM NATIONAL JURISDICTION TO THE AREA: WHY SPILLOVER MATTERS The distinction between Ghana’s continental shelf and the Area makes the environmental question particularly important because, within its continental shelf, Ghana exercises sovereign rights over seabed resources. Beyond the outer limit of national jurisdiction, however, the seabed becomes part of the Area, where no State possesses sovereignty and the resources are governed under the common-heritage regime. An environmental effect originating within Ghana’s jurisdiction can nevertheless move beyond that jurisdiction. Where pollution, sediment plumes, ecological disturbance or other significant effects reach marine environments beyond national jurisdiction, the matter ceases to be exclusively domestic in character. It engages international environmental interests and potentially international obligations. The delimitation of jurisdiction therefore determines who has authority over the resource, but it does not create an ecological barrier capable of containing environmental effects. BBNJ: WHEN EFFECTS CROSS THE JURISDICTIONAL LINE The BBNJ Agreement principally concerns marine biological diversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, and it does not displace Ghana’s sovereign rights within its EEZ or continental shelf. However, its EIA provisions recognise that activities conducted under national jurisdiction or control may have environmental consequences beyond national jurisdiction. Part IV, Articles 27–39, establishes a detailed framework covering screening, scoping, impact assessment, consultation, mitigation, decision-making, monitoring, reporting and review. Of particular importance, Article 28 addresses planned activities under the jurisdiction or control of a Party that may have effects in areas beyond national jurisdiction, creating an important connection between domestic assessment and international responsibility. If an offshore activity authorised by Ghana remains environmentally confined within national jurisdiction, Ghana’s domestic legal framework and applicable UNCLOS obligations provide the principal regulatory basis. If its potential effects extend into areas beyond national jurisdiction, however, the international dimension becomes materially stronger. This is precisely why a robust EIA should be undertaken before activity begins: assessment should identify potential pathways and geographical reach of impacts rather than wait until environmental effects cross the jurisdictional boundary. Tanaka (2024), analysing the BBNJ EIA regime in Ocean Development & International Law, emphasises its preventive character and its importance where marine biodiversity damage may be difficult to reverse. CUMULATIVE IMPACTS: THE OCEAN IS ALREADY UNDER PRESSURE The proposed reconnaissance activity will not enter an unused marine environment. Ghana’s waters already support fisheries, shipping and offshore petroleum activities and are exposed to pollution, climate-related pressures and other human impacts. Owusu, Lawer, Adjei and Ogbe (2023) document conflicts between offshore petroleum development and small-scale fisheries in Ghana, particularly over access to marine space and coastal livelihoods. Adjei and Overå (2019) similarly demonstrate that tensions between extractive industries and fisheries have already emerged in Ghana’s offshore development experience. These findings strengthen the case for cumulative impact assessment. The relevant question is not only what one reconnaissance operation may do in isolation, but what its impacts may become when combined with existing and reasonably foreseeable pressures on the same marine ecosystem. FROM REGULATORY SILOS TO INTEGRATED OCEAN GOVERNANCE The Fisheries Commission’s proposal for inter-agency review should therefore be supported. A significant offshore activity may simultaneously engage mineral resources, fisheries, biodiversity, navigation, pollution prevention, maritime safety and coastal livelihoods. No single regulator possesses all the necessary expertise. Ghana should institutionalise an Inter-Agency Marine Environmental Assessment and Ocean Governance Mechanism, drawing upon the mandates of the Fisheries Commission, Minerals Commission, Environmental Protection Authority, Ghana Maritime Authority and other competent institutions. Its purpose should be practical: coordinated screening and scoping, marine and fisheries baselines, cumulative-impact assessment, stakeholder consultation, data sharing, mitigation, emergency planning, monitoring and adaptive management. CONCLUSION Ghana possesses clear sovereign rights over offshore mineral resources. UNCLOS Articles 56 and 77 establish those rights within the EEZ and continental shelf, respectively. Article 76 establishes the legal framework for the outer continental shelf, while the Area beyond national jurisdiction is governed by UNCLOS Part XI as the common heritage of mankind. But the boundary separating national jurisdiction from the global commons is a legal boundary, not an environmental wall. UNCLOS Articles 192-194 require protection of the marine environment, while Article 206 requires environmental assessment where the prescribed risk threshold is met. Ghana’s Fisheries and Aquaculture Act, 2025 (Act 1146), provides the domestic fisheries-assessment dimension, while BBNJ Part IV strengthens the international framework where activities may affect marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction. Finally, Ghana has the sovereign right to explore its offshore resources, but it must assess and manage the environmental consequences of exercising that right, including consequences capable of extending beyond national jurisdiction. This is particularly important because once significant effects cross into areas beyond national jurisdiction, the environmental consequences are no longer exclusively Ghana’s concern. The appropriate approach is therefore neither prohibition nor unqualified exploitation. It is assessment before authorisation, coordination before conflict, and prevention before remediation. That is the standard required for credible ocean governance.

items.title: Man United legend Patrice Evra announces mum’s death
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Manchester United and France defender Patrice Evra has announced the death of his mother, Juliette, following her battle with Alzheimer’s disease. Evra shared the heartbreaking news in an emotional video posted on his social media accounts, where he paid tribute to his mother while singing “Avant qu’elle parte” by French hip-hop group Sexion d’Assaut. The former defender struggled to hold back his emotions before addressing his followers. “I lost my rock, but I’m trying to stay positive. People ask me every time if I’m always happy,” Evra said. “And now all the people that have still got their mum, even if death doesn’t stop the love, just tell them you love them every single day, before they leave.” Evra also accompanied the video with a heartfelt message celebrating his mother’s love. “Even when the whole world is against you, she will always be your best friend. “A mother’s love is forever, no matter what happens in life. Rest in peace, Maman. You will always be in my heart,” he wrote. The 45-year-old had previously spoken publicly about his mother’s health struggles and the profound impact she had on his life. Evra has also used his social media posts to pay tribute to Juliette by occasionally appearing in videos wearing only one shoe. He revealed that the gesture was dedicated to his mother, who lost her left leg after being rushed to hospital in 2010. Speaking about the incident, Evra recalled receiving the news while he was away with the France national team. He travelled to the hospital after seeking permission from the team’s manager and later discovered that his mother had lost her leg. “When I arrived in the corridor, everyone was crying. I saw my brother and sister. I said, ‘Wow, this is weird,’” he recalled. “Then I went to the room. My mum was on the bed and I kissed her. Then I sat next to her. It was only when I pulled off the blanket, that’s when I saw the left leg was missing.” Evra said his decision to leave his left shoe off in some of his videos was his way of keeping his mother’s memory close. “Every time I do a video, I just dedicate it to my hero, my mum,” he said. The post Man United legend Patrice Evra announces mum’s death appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le FLA annonce un « retrait stratégique » de la ville de Kidal
items.description: Le Front de libération de l'Azawad a annoncé avoir procédé à « un retrait stratégique et discipliné de ses forces de la ville de Kidal », précisant que cette décision intervenait « face aux risques croissants qui menacent le reste de la population civile de la ville, en raison de l'utilisation excessive de moyens aériens » par les Russes rattachés à la Force africaine en Afrique et les forces maliennes. Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi, le FLA a déclaré que cette décision résultait « d’une évaluation objective de la situation opérationnelle et tactique, et visait avant tout à préserver la vie des civils, face à un ennemi qui évite tout affrontement terrestre direct. » Selon le Front, les opérations aériennes ont « entraîné la destruction de la majeure partie des infrastructures publiques et civiles, et mis en danger la vie de civils innocents, que le régime de Bamako prend systématiquement pour cible ». Il a précisé que « cette mesure est une mesure opérationnelle temporaire, visant également à préserver ses capacités humaines et logistiques en pleine état de préparation. Ce retrait organisé de la ville s’est déroulé sans que les forces du Front n’aient, jusqu’à présent, engagé de confrontation directe. » Le Front de libération de l’Azawad affirme que « sa lutte se poursuivra avec constance et détermination » ajoutant que « Les mercenaires russes se heurteront à la volonté des fils de l’Azawad, qui resteront prêts à défendre leur terre, leur dignité, leurs droits et l’avenir de leur peuple. » Le Front avait pris le contrôle de Kidal à la suite d’opérations coordonnées lancées le 25 avril dernier, avec le soutien du groupe « Nasra al-Islam wa al-Muslimin » (Défense de l’islam et des musulmans), lié à Al-Qaïda. L’armée malienne a annoncé ce mardi le lancement d’opérations de grande envergure dans toute la région de Kidal.

items.title: Teacher unions maintain strike as FWSC, GES negotiations yield no deal
items.description: The nationwide strike by pre-tertiary teachers remains in force after renewed negotiations between the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC), the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the teacher unions ended without an agreement. The parties are expected to reconvene on Wednesday, October 7 as government continues efforts to address the concerns that triggered the industrial action. A key issue under discussion is the processing of outstanding data for teachers who have been promoted, which is necessary for the payment of their related promotion arrears. Speaking to the media after Tuesday’s meeting, General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), Thomas Musa, urged teachers to remain resolute as the unions await concrete timelines from government. He said the unions were expecting clear commitments on when the outstanding processes would be completed and when affected teachers would receive their payments. The latest meeting forms part of efforts to resolve the dispute and restore teaching and learning in pre-tertiary schools across the country. The unions have been pressing government to address outstanding financial obligations owed to teachers, including promotion arrears and other concerns relating to their conditions of service. The strike has disrupted academic activities in public pre-tertiary schools, with the unions insisting that concrete measures and timelines are required before they consider suspending the action. Government has maintained that it is committed to resolving the concerns and has been engaging the unions through the FWSC and the GES. The Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, had earlier appealed to the striking teachers to return to the classroom, saying the government was committed to finding an amicable resolution to their concerns. He also announced that the 20 per cent deprived-area allowance would be paid after the validation of teachers eligible for the allowance is completed. With Tuesday’s negotiations ending without an agreement, attention now turns to Wednesday’s meeting, where the unions are expected to seek clearer timelines from government on the outstanding processes and payments.

items.title: France test-fires new nuclear-capable missile – Defence ministry
items.description: France on Tuesday fired for the first time its new M51.3 nuclear-capable ballistic missile from a nuclear-powered submarine, a successful test that President Emmanuel Macron argued showed the credibility of the French nuclear deterrent. The missile, a variant of France’s M51 missile and which was not carrying a warhead, was fired from the Le Vigilant submarine off Brittany and impacted “in the North Atlantic, hundreds of kilometres (miles) from any coastline”, the defence ministry said. Macron witnessed the firing aboard French warship Auvergne, posting a video on X showing the missile arching up into the sky after its launch. “To be free, one must be feared. And to be feared, one must be powerful,” Macron wrote on X. “This technical success further demonstrates the credibility of our nuclear deterrent, whose long-term viability is assured,” he added. The defence ministry emphasised the launch was conducted without a nuclear warhead and “in strict compliance with France’s international commitments”. The test “once again demonstrates the excellence of the high-tech solutions employed by French industry in the field of nuclear deterrence”, it said. Macron warned of a shift in the nature of “Russian aggression and threats” against European nations following a series of “hybrid” attacks blamed on Moscow. He vowed in mid-September that these actions would “not go unanswered”. The French president also proposed this year that European partners join the “advanced” nuclear deterrence framework of France, the European Union’s sole nuclear weapons power. “Our nuclear deterrent protects us and will continue to protect us,” he argued. The post France test-fires new nuclear-capable missile – Defence ministry appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Paramount takes over Warner Bros in $110bn Hollywood merger
items.description: Paramount Skydance has officially taken over Warner Bros Discovery in a $110bn merger that is set to reshape Hollywood and the media landscape. The takeover – merging two of the biggest studios in Los Angeles – comes after months of legal disputes and widespread criticism over feared cuts and consolidation could harm competition and consumers. It will alter streaming for millions, usher in a new chapter in the film and TV industry, and leave one of the biggest US news outlets, CNN, in uncertain territory. The merger will also bring together a host of entities including HBO, CBS, Nickelodeon, Showtime, Comedy Central, DC Studios and Food Network. Paramount will acquire ownership of iconic franchises that include Harry Potter, Game of Thrones, The Lord of the Rings and Mission: Impossible. The newly merged entertainment behemoth will be re-branded under the name Skydance Corporation, the company originally founded by David Ellison before he took over both Paramount and Warner Bros Discover. Ellison, chairman and chief executive of Skydance, said the completion of the deal was “historic” for the film industry. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality,” he said. Last week, Ellison named the outgoing chief executive of Mattel, Ynon Kreiz, as co-chief executive. Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day operations, including integrating the newly-combined businesses, while Ellison will focus on strategy and technology. Mark Thompson – who once served as director general of the BBC – will continue in his role as chairman and editor-in-chief of CNN Worldwide, while Bari Weiss remains editor-in-chief of CBS News. Casey Bloys, who has lead HBO and Max Content, will be the co-chair and chief content officer for direct-to-consumer content. Mike Proulx, research director at Forrester Research, said that change “essentially means the HBO leadership team is now in charge of Skydance’s combined streaming operation”. “While that bodes well for the HBO brand, make no mistake, Bloys will be pressured to find and deliver cost efficiencies that could affect content quality,” he warned. Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said the company has high debts at a time when interest rates are high. “The combined entity, now called Skydance, needs to cut costs and make bigger profits to be able to get the debt down to more manageable levels,” he said. “The fact Tom Cruise movie Digger, Warner Bros’ last release before the merger, has been a major flop is a reminder of how the film industry is not a guaranteed ticket to riches.” Rocky path to merger While the company said it had received unanimous approval from competition authorities across the world, the long running takeover process has featured controversy since the beginning. Netflix initially had a deal to buy part of Warner Bros Discovery, but Paramount Skydance launched a bidding war, leading to the streaming giant walking away. Lawyers in about a dozen US states then filed lawsuits – led by California – aiming to block the deal, arguing it would stifle competition, raise consumer prices and cause “substantial” harm to movie theatres, cable distributors and “ultimately, audiences nationwide”. US states announced a settlement with Paramount and Ellison last month which paved the way for the merger to go ahead . As part of the deal, Paramount has agreed to establish a “news editorial independence board” to “ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting” at CNN and CBS. Politics and editorial independence has become an area of concern at CBS since the news broadcaster was taken over in 2025 as part of separate a merger between Skydance Media and Paramount. Ellison, who hosted a dinner for President Donald Trump earlier this year, has sought to reassure people that editorial independence will be maintained. Over its 103-year-old history, Warner Bros has won more than 100 Academy Awards – including dominating at last year’s show with a record-tying 11 Oscars for One Battle After Another, Sinners and Weapons. Paramount traces its roots back 1912 and also boasts more than 100 Oscars for classics spanning from The Godfather to Titanic, though the studio has not mirrored the same recent spate of Hollywood honours. The studio was not nominated for any projects last year by the Academy. Its last win came in 2022 with Top Gun: Maverick. The deal with US states aims to ensure the merged studios will produce “real, robust movies” that will generate economic activity and put people back to work, said California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the lawsuit and settlement. To prevent the studio from fulfilling its annual quota with low-budget or automated content, the deal includes strict guardrails against “AI-generated” films. As part of the agreement, Paramount must release at least 30 films each year. If it fails to meet its annual production quota, it will be forced to sell its 49% stake in Miramax, the film company founded by disgraced Hollywood mogul Harvey Weinstein and his brother Bob. Paramount also must ensure 20% of all film production takes place in the US for the first two years, rising to more than 30% through the following three years.

items.title: Photos: Mahama Ayariga engages World Bank on sustainable cities development
items.description: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has held an engagement with the World Bank on sustainable cities development as Ghana seeks to strengthen urban planning and infrastructure to meet the demands of rapid urbanisation. The engagement, held on Tuesday, October 6, focused on strategies to build cities that are better planned, more resilient and inclusive, while improving their ability to respond to the growing challenges associated with urbanisation. Mr Ayariga said the cities being built today would have a significant impact on the opportunities, quality of life and prospects of future generations. “The cities we build today will shape the opportunities, quality of life, and future of generations to come.” He said discussions with the World Bank explored practical opportunities to strengthen urban infrastructure and improve service delivery, while deepening collaboration in support of sustainable development. “I had a productive engagement with the World Bank on sustainable cities development, focusing on how we can build cities that are better planned, more resilient, inclusive and equipped to respond to the challenges of rapid urbanisation.” According to the Minister, the discussions also centred on practical measures to improve the delivery of essential services and create urban environments that can better withstand emerging challenges. “Our discussions explored practical opportunities to strengthen urban infrastructure, improve service delivery, and deepen collaboration in support of sustainable development.” Mr Ayariga stressed the importance of partnerships with development institutions such as the World Bank in translating Ghana’s urban development ambitions into practical outcomes that directly benefit communities. “Strong partnerships with institutions such as the World Bank are critical to turning these ambitions into tangible outcomes for our communities.” He expressed optimism about sustained collaboration with the World Bank as the government works towards developing cities that are more functional, inclusive and responsive to the needs of residents. “I look forward to continued engagement and collaboration towards building cities that work better for everyone.” See more photos below:

items.title: Foreign Affairs Minister warns embassies over long queues, ‘inhumane’ conditions for visa applicants
items.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has warned embassies and consulates in Ghana against subjecting Ghanaian visa applicants to long queues, delays and what he describes as inhumane conditions. The Minister said the government expects Ghanaian citizens seeking visas to be treated with dignity and respect throughout the application process. Mr Ablakwa made the comments after visiting about 20 embassies and assessing the conditions under which Ghanaians apply for visas. He said although the majority of diplomatic missions have improved their services, concerns remain about the treatment of applicants at some embassies, particularly regarding long waiting periods. “The Ministry of Foreign Affairs expects the citizens of our country are treated with dignity, with respect, that our citizens do not go through humiliation and disrespect and inhumane conditions when they are applying for visas,” he said. He said he intends to engage ambassadors and high commissioners of countries where concerns have been identified to discuss the issues and seek improvements. “There are some countries that will have to improve their services, and I intend inviting those ambassadors.” According to the Minister, he has already raised the issue with one ambassador during his recent visit, while engagements with other diplomatic missions are expected to follow. “The government of Ghana will insist that all visa applicants are treated with respect, with dignity, and that their concerns are taken on board and are not treated with contempt,” he stressed.

items.title: Photos: AMA steps up enforcement to clear traders from BRT shelters
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has stepped up efforts to remove traders and other commercial operators who have occupied Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) shelters in parts of the capital. The exercise is aimed at restoring the shelters to their intended purpose and improving movement for pedestrians, commuters and motorists. The latest operation was carried out on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, at the Aayalolo BRT bus shelter near the former Telecel office at the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange. The exercise was led by the Mayor of Accra, Hon. Michael Kpakpo Allotey, who was accompanied by the Coordinating and Finance Directors and members of the Assembly’s enforcement team. Traders had occupied sections of the shelter and were using the space to sell mobile phones, accessories and other items, limiting access for commuters who were expected to use the facility. Despite the rainfall, the enforcement team proceeded with the exercise and removed tables and other items that had been placed within the shelter. Speaking to the traders during the operation, Mayor Allotey explained that the exercise was not intended to target individuals or take away their means of livelihood. He said the action was necessary to restore order, protect commuters and ensure that public infrastructure was used for the purpose for which it was constructed. The Mayor also pointed to the immediate improvement in movement after the shelter was cleared, saying it demonstrated the effect that unauthorised trading had on access to the facility and the flow of traffic in the area. According to him, commuters who should have been using the designated bus stop were being forced onto the road because traders had taken over parts of the shelter. He said this created additional risks for pedestrians and motorists, particularly at a busy location such as the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange. The AMA says the enforcement exercise forms part of broader efforts to reclaim public spaces and ensure that facilities provided for public use remain accessible. The Assembly is expected to continue the exercise at other BRT shelters across the metropolis as it works to prevent commercial activities from interfering with commuter access and the smooth movement of traffic.

items.title: Shortage of health information officers threatens quality of healthcare data – GHIMA
items.description: The Ghana Health Information Management Association (GHIMA) has warned that the absence of health information officers in some health facilities threatens the quality, reliability, and timely availability of data needed to save lives and improve healthcare delivery. The situation risks undermining critical decisions on patient care, resource allocation and health policy, leaving healthcare managers to operate without the accurate information required to address pressing health challenges. President of the Ghana Health Information Management Association (GHIMA), Richard Delali Ahedor, says the situation is unacceptable, insisting qualified health information officers will ensure proper data management. Health information is an essential element in healthcare delivery which aids decisions on patient treatment, planning, monitoring, research, resource allocation and policy development depending on the availability of accurate and timely data. However, in many health facilities across the country, professionally trained personnel are either inadequate, or are lacking. President of the Ghana Health Information Management Association (GHIMA), Richard Delali Ahedor says addressing the concerns called on the government for immediate recruitment complemented with essential infrastructure and equipment supply. “This is unacceptable; inadequacy will lead to poor quality of information management, timeliness, consistency, and adequacy. All of those factors will be compromised. “We are appealing to the government to look at the issue. All facilities should have such officers. Even the facilities that have, don’t have computers, sitting positions, offices to manage the facilities. So, recruitment won’t be enough, unless all complementary resources are also provided,” he said. The national president made the remarks at the maiden Regional General Meeting of the Ashanti Regional Chapter of GHIMA, held under the theme, “Implementation of the Ghana Health Information Management System (GHIMS): The Role of the Health Information Practitioner.” Regional Governor of the Ashanti Regional Chapter of GHIMA, Augustine Agyeman, indicated the chapter remains committed to professional development to strengthen the profession. He says that the successful implementation of the Ghana Health Information Management System would require skilled personnel and professional commitment besides technological investment. “Technology alone cannot guarantee the success of the system. The competence, commitment, and professionalism remain fundamental to the successful implementation and sustainability. “it’s important to demonstrate the value of health information management in improving healthcare delivery. It also challenges us to upgrade our knowledge and skills in digital health, information systems, data quality management and emerging technologies,” he said. Meanwhile, Regional Health Information Officer, Kennedy Nartey, presenting the 2026 Ashanti Regional Health Profile, urged practitioners to make greater use of the data they collect to identify gaps and improve service delivery. He encouraged health information officers to go beyond data collection and reporting by analysing and applying the information to guide improvements in healthcare services. “Challenges like lack of registers and non-comprehensive electronic systems, Incomplete data, stress from some private facilities, some services, Data quality at all levels, Inadequate staff and Poor data use. “We must encourage ourselves to use the data as officers in health. We can assure ourselves that we have quality data and, based on that, we can come up with improvements,” he said.

items.title: 10 things to know about the viral Lagos Life game
items.description: Lagos Life game, a Nigerian-made browser game that turns everyday Lagos experiences into a virtual life simulation, has gone viral just days after its launch, attracting more than one million players and sparking conversations across social media. Called Lagos Life, the game allows users to create characters, find jobs, earn virtual naira, rent homes, socialise, visit familiar Lagos locations and compete with other players in a shared virtual city. Here are 10 things to know about the game. 1. Lagos Life is basically “The Sims” set in Lagos Lagos Life is a life-simulation game that takes the concept popularised by The Sims and places it in a Nigerian setting. Instead of living in a fictional suburb, players navigate a virtual Lagos where they can work, earn money, pay rent, socialise, go out and build their virtual lives. The developer says the game is inspired by different aspects of Nigerian life, including employment, finance, property, transportation, entertainment, relationships, government and social activities. 2. It was created by Nigerian developer Shalom Rayhamen The game was created by Nigerian software developer Shalom Rayhamen, who operates under the name Eliy. Rayhamen has said the idea was influenced by her experience playing The Sims 3 and wondering what the game would look like if it reflected the environment and culture she knew. The viral Lagos Run danfo-driving game also helped inspire the project. 3. It launched on October 1, 2026 Lagos Life went live on October 1, Nigeria’s Independence Day, and its growth was almost immediate. Techpoint Africa reported that the game’s dashboard showed more than 1.2 million total players and over 71,000 people online by October 5, alongside more than 9.6 million all-time visits. The developer had also reported a peak of more than 109,000 players online at once. The figures come primarily from the game’s own dashboard, so they have not been independently audited. 4. You don’t need to download an app One of Lagos Life’s biggest advantages is its accessibility. It is played directly through a web browser , meaning users do not need to download a large game or install an application before playing. The game can be accessed from phones and computers, making it considerably easier for people to try compared with games that require consoles, gaming PCs or large mobile downloads. 5. Players have to make a living The game isn’t simply about walking around a virtual Lagos. Players have to manage their virtual lives by working jobs, earning money, spending money and paying rent. There are multiple career paths, with jobs ranging from banking and technology to entertainment and other professions. Players can progress through different levels of their careers as they develop their characters. In other words, the game turns familiar Lagos struggles — getting a job, making money and paying the landlord — into gameplay. 6. The game has recognisable Lagos locations Lagos Life deliberately uses locations and experiences that Nigerians can recognise. Players can visit places including Amala Shitta and Quilox, while other aspects of the game draw from Lagos transport, nightlife, food and popular culture. That local detail is an important part of its appeal because the game isn’t simply a generic life simulator with Nigerian names added to it. Its gameplay is built around experiences that are familiar to its target audience. 7. The virtual money is not real money One of the biggest misconceptions surrounding Lagos Life is that players can make money they can eventually withdraw. They cannot. The game’s terms state that its in-game naira, properties, items and jobs have no real-world value and cannot be cashed out or transferred outside the game. Players can purchase in-game naira using real money, but the virtual currency itself cannot be withdrawn as cash. So, despite the game’s focus on jobs and money, it should not be treated as an investment or money-making platform. 8. Businesses can advertise inside the virtual Lagos Lagos Life is not relying entirely on players to generate revenue. The developer has created a form of virtual real estate where businesses can pay to advertise inside the game. According to Techpoint Africa, companies can rent virtual billboards and plots in the game, with some businesses already using the space to promote their brands. This means Lagos Life is effectively turning its virtual city into an advertising platform as its audience grows. 9. It is designed for adults Despite its cartoon-like appearance, Lagos Life is officially an 18+ game. Its terms of service state that users must be at least 18 years old to create an account. The requirement is particularly relevant because the game involves interaction between real players, including chat and social activities. The developer’s rules prohibit harassment, threats, hate speech, sexual content, scams and the sharing of private information. 10. Its success could be bigger than just a viral game Perhaps the most interesting thing about Lagos Life is what its sudden popularity says about Nigerian digital entertainment. The game has demonstrated how quickly a locally relevant product can attract an audience when it combines familiar culture, humour, accessibility and social interaction. Its rise also follows the viral success of Lagos Run, another Nigerian browser game in which players drive a yellow danfo through Lagos traffic. That game was released only days before Lagos Life and helped trigger a wave of interest in Nigerian-themed browser games. The post 10 things to know about the viral Lagos Life game appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana’s National Chess Team, The Golden Knights return from Samarkand with gold and seven new international titles
items.description: Ghana’s national chess team, the Golden Knights, has returned from the 46th World Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan with a gold medal and seven new international titles, the best result the country has ever recorded at the event. The Ghana women’s team finished top of rating Category D to take gold, playing in board order Maud Benson, Gertrude Banini, Ridham, Dzidzor Dotse and Sumya Ibrahim Dotse. Seven Ghanaian players earned FIDE titles over the course of the tournament. Bernard Anhwere earned the FIDE Master title. Price Akpa and Dr Daniel Mensah Loglo, both of the open section, earned the Candidate Master title. Maud Benson earned the Woman FIDE Master title, and Sumya Ibrahim Dotse, Ridham and Dzidzor Esi Dotse each earned the Woman Candidate Master title. The delegation was led by Madam Christiana Ashley, President of the Ghana Chess Association, who served as Head of Delegation. Samarkand was her first Olympiad since taking office earlier this year, and the campaign reflected the preparation and organization she put in place on assuming the presidency: an earlier and clearer selection process, structured training ahead of departure, and a delegation that arrived in Uzbekistan ready to play. This result belongs to the players. They did the work at the board. What we set out to do when I took office was make sure that when Ghanaian players sit down against the rest of the world, nothing about their preparation is left to chance. Seven titles and a gold medal tell me we are on the right road, and I want us to go further.” — Madam Christiana Ashley, President, Ghana Chess Association. The Association also credits the coaching and technical team, the team captains, and the officials who supported the squad in Samarkand and in the months of preparation before it. The Golden Knights leave Samarkand with Ghana’s strongest Olympiad record to date and a larger pool of titled players than the country has ever had. The GCA thanks Ghanaians at home and abroad who followed the team round by round, and says the work now turns to youth development and to defending this standard at the next Olympiad. Ghana to the world.

Djokovic wins China Open, keeps unbeaten record after opponent retires
items.description: Novak Djokovic won the China Open on Tuesday after his opponent Alex de Minaur retired from the final, extending an astonishing unbeaten streak in Beijing and winning the 102nd title of his career. The 39-year-old Serbian won the first set in the tie-break 7-6 (7/3) and was down a game in the second set when the Australian ended the match early. “I always want to visualise myself with the trophy, particularly here in Beijing,” Djokovic said during the trophy ceremony. “But I was also quite aware that reality is a little bit different these days,” he said, adding that it had been a challenging year with “physical and health issues”. “I was just trying to find the good feeling on the court,” he said. The first set was a physical battle that lasted more than one hour, and both men needed medical timeouts before the second. De Minaur, the world number nine, won the first game of the second set before retiring. It was not immediately clear why de Minaur left the match, but he walked back onto the court after his medical timeout with a white wrap around his left thigh. “I don’t feel great,” de Minaur told the crowd afterwards. “I want to say sorry to the amazing fans that came to watch… I didn’t want to finish like this,” the 27-year-old added. De Minaur advanced to the final after his opponent Hubert Hurkacz retired injured from their semi-final on Monday, while Djokovic moved through when Daniil Medvedev was disqualified for hitting a fan with a ball. With the win, Djokovic extended a perfect record to 34 wins in as many matches for his seventh title in the Chinese capital — his first since 2015. He put on a valiant show to lift the trophy, ousting top seed Alexander Zverev in the quarter-final and coming back to defeat home hopeful Bu Yunchaokete in a demanding three sets. Djokovic, a 24-time Grand Slam champion, will finish the season with a title for the 21st consecutive year. – ‘Really grateful’ – In the women’s draw, Karolina Muchova beat former world number one Naomi Osaka on her ninth match point to reach the quarter-finals, triumphant in a tense tie-break. Muchova, the seventh seed, overcame 50 unforced errors across the two-hour-and-52-minute match to beat Osaka 7-5, 1-6, 7-6 (9/7). Osaka, who represents Japan, saved eight match points but could not get past Muchova’s match-winning volley. “I was shaking. I’m happy I made the last volley… Naomi could be standing here. It’s me, and I’m really grateful for it,” the 30-year-old Czech player told the crowd. She next faces compatriot Nikola Bartunkova. Earlier, Russia’s Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine’s Daria Snigur 6-2, 6-2 to book her quarter-final spot against fellow Russian Ekaterina Alexandrova. Alexandrova, ranked 28th, upset Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2, 6-2, ending the Czech player’s bid to return to the Beijing final that she reached last year. AFP The post Djokovic wins China Open, keeps unbeaten record after opponent retires appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: We need our full budget to ensure seamless polls, INEC cries out
items.description: …We’ve no candidates in Nigeria’s elections – EU …Explains how it will use AI during election …To deploy 1,414,768 ad hoc staff By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has asked the Federal Government to promptly release the remaining part of its budget, saying it is needed to deliver the 2027 General Election seamlessly. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash O. Amupitan SAN, made the appeal on Tuesday at a World Press Conference and National Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abuja, held to mark 100 days to the first ballot. “We expect the prompt release of the remaining budget to ensure seamless execution of the remaining activities,” Amupitan said. He, however, acknowledged that “the Federal Government has maintained its commitment to democratic governance through the timely release of statutory budgetary allocations to the Commission.” According to him, the funds have enabled INEC to “meet international vendor obligations, finance the production of critical election technology, upgrade physical infrastructure, and sustain multi-stakeholder operational deployments nationwide.” ‘EU has no candidate’ The Ambassador of the European Union EU to Nigeria and the Economic Community of West African States ECOWAS, Mr Gautier Mignot, backed the call, urging all actors “to facilitate as much as possible the work of INEC, not least from a budgetary point of view.” “This is a Herculean task,” Mignot said. He also made clear where the EU stands. “Ours is a friendly partnership, respectful of Nigerian sovereignty. We don’t impose any view or orientation. And needless to say, we don’t support specific candidates or parties,” he said. Mignot said the EU would deploy an electoral mission of experts to follow the run-up to the election, the conduct of the ballot and its aftermath, and “come back in due time with recommendations.” AI integration On technology, Amupitan disclosed that INEC has set up a dedicated Artificial Intelligence AI Division within its Information and Communication Technology ICT Department. He said, “Automated AI auditing tools are being integrated into our results verification process under a five-pillar AI Governance Framework, operating under mandatory human oversight. ” A governance policy, he added, “is being finalised by the Commission.” The chairman said INEC is also integrating “AI-driven anomaly detection tools to monitor database traffic and shield our public portals against cyber intrusions or unauthorised alterations.” Amupitan warned that generative AI, voice cloning and deepfake videos “now make it cheap to fabricate the voices of election officials, doctored result sheets and fake letterheads, and to spread them faster than they can be verified.” He urged the media to set up fact-checking desks and verify with INEC before publishing. “In national elections, it is far more important to be right than to be first,” he said. 1.4m ad hoc staff On manpower, the chairman said INEC will need 707,384 ad hoc personnel for the Presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16 and the same number for the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. “That is a total of 1,414,768 engagements across 176,846 polling units, compared with about 1.2 million in 2023,” he said. The bulk of the workforce will again come from the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). Amupitan recalled that in 2023, “more than 70 per cent of our ad hoc staff, nearly 850,000 people, were corps members and student volunteers.” He said the INEC Portal for Recruitment of Election Staff opened on September 18 and closes at midnight on November 18. The chairman said the National Register of Voters now stands at 103 million, following the registration of 10,772,421 new voters in three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration. The register will be displayed for public scrutiny from October 9 to 15, while distribution of Phase 1 Permanent Voter Cards PVCs to local government centres begins on Friday, October 9. He added that 18 of the 22 registered political parties submitted candidates for the presidential election. Amupitan disclosed that INEC received the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment in INEC v. Zenith Labour Party only on Tuesday morning and is reviewing it. The Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Electoral Matters, Hon. Adebayo Balogun, said the committee had written INEC “to enforce the judgment of the Supreme Court on the Section 74 of the Electoral Act.” “Just like the governors who decide or shy away from signing death warrants, which is their right and duty, INEC too is also mandated to take action where necessary,” Balogun said. The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Electoral Matters, Sen. Simon Lalong, said “the credibility of an election is the responsibility” of political parties, candidates, security agencies, the media, civil society and voters. Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) Francis Idu of the Police Mobile Force, who represented the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Disu, said clearance operations were ongoing in Kogi, Niger, Benue and Taraba states “to quell the various crisis points and ensure there is social harmony for the election.” The National Chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council IPAC, Yusuf Mamman Dantalle, commended INEC over the Osun State governorship election but warned its officials “not to take sides with any political party or any candidate.” He asked INEC to “engage more before election with the political parties” and told stakeholders, “This election will come and go, but Nigeria will remain.” The post 2027: We need our full budget to ensure seamless polls, INEC cries out appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NAF aircraft crash: Senate postpones security summit to honour victims
items.description: By Henry Umoru The Senate has postponed its planned two-day National Security Summit, earlier scheduled for Monday, 12th and Tuesday, 13th October, 2026, until further notice. The upper chamber postponed the summit consequent upon the tragic crash of a Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area, Ondo State, which claimed the lives of 25 officers and seven crew members on Monday. In a statement he personally signed on Tuesday, the Leader of the Senate and Chairman, Senate Ad-hoc Committee on the National Security Summit, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, said that a new date for the summit would be communicated in due course, thereby appealing to all the stakeholders “to take note of the national disaster and bear with the Senate during this period of national mourning.” The Senate had convened the security summit to review the country’s perennial security challenges and propose pragmatic solutions that could guarantee security of lives and property across the federation. According to Bamidele, the ad hoc committee had already concluded the plan to hold the summit after the completion of zonal public hearings, but the crash of the NAF ATR-42 aircraft suddenly necessitated the postponement of the national security summit on Monday. President Bola Tinubu consequently declared three days of national mourning in honour of 25 officers and seven crew members of the Nigerian Air Force and directed that the national flags be flown at half-mast nationwide. The Senate Leader said that against the backdrop of the declaration of national mourning, the Senate resolved that the national security summit should be deferred till further notice in honour of the victims of the crash. The Senate also extended its heartfelt condolences “to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR; the Nigerian Armed Forces, particularly the Nigerian Air Force; and the families of the gallant officers and crew members who paid the supreme price in active service to the fatherland.” The post NAF aircraft crash: Senate postpones security summit to honour victims appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Northern Births and Deaths Director to face PAC over withdrawals totalling GH¢71k
items.description: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has summoned the Northern Regional Director of the Births and Deaths Registry to explain withdrawals totalling GH¢71,300 made without payment vouchers and the required supporting documents. The withdrawals, made between March 12, 2024, and October 22, 2025, came under scrutiny when agencies under the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs appeared before the Committee on Tuesday, October 6. The Committee raised concerns over several transactions, including withdrawals of GH¢15,800 and GH¢18,000, for which the required documentation was not available. PAC members questioned the Registrar of the Births and Deaths Registry, Samuel Adom Botchway, about the circumstances surrounding the withdrawals and measures taken to ensure compliance with financial procedures. Mr Botchway initially told the Committee that the outstanding issues had been addressed through payment vouchers and memoranda submitted for approval. However, the Committee stressed that producing the documents after the transactions did not resolve concerns over whether the required procedures had been followed before the public funds were withdrawn. The Committee subsequently directed the Northern Regional Director to appear before it together with Mr Botchway by Friday to provide explanations on the transactions. “So we will step it down for now. We sit from today to the 20th. We’ll give you up to Friday for him to come with you and discharge his mandate,” Chairperson of the Committee, Abena Osei Asare, said. Mr Botchway subsequently apologised to the Committee and agreed to bring the Regional Director to answer questions on the withdrawals.

items.title: Djokovic claims 102nd title of career with China Open win
items.description: Novak Djokovic claimed the 102nd title of his astonishing career as Alex de Minaur retired injured from the China Open final. The 39-year-old led De Minaur – a player 12 years his junior – 7-6 (7-3) 0-1 when the Australian was forced to quit with an apparent left thigh problem. It is the 21st year in a row that Djokovic has won at least one singles title. Only Jimmy Connors (109) and Roger Federer (103) have won more singles titles in their careers than the Serb. The 24-time Grand Slam champion was competing in only his second final of the year after losing January’s Australian Open showpiece to Carlos Alcaraz. Djokovic beat world number two Alexander Zverev on his way to the Beijing final and was a set and a break up on third seed Daniil Medvedev when the Russian was defaulted from their semi-final. Djokovic is on a 34-match winning streak at the China Open, having claimed the trophy seven times. Earlier, Alcaraz won the Japan Open, claiming a trophy in just his third tournament since injuring his wrist in April. The Spaniard came back from an early break down to beat Czech Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7-4) 6-4 and successfully defend his title in Tokyo. Alcaraz only returned to competitive tennis at August’s US Open, where he reached the quarter-finals before losing in five tight sets to Ben Shelton. It is Alcaraz’s third title of the season, having won the Australian Open in January to complete the career Grand Slam, and also February’s Qatar Open. “It’s extra special after my injury,” the 25-year-old said. “It was a tough week that I didn’t find my best tennis, my best level, but I did find the good solutions. “I think that’s what matters in the end.”

items.title: Desire FC teams up with Hellas Verona to develop emerging talent in Ghana
items.description: Ghanaian Youth Football Academy Desire Football Club have formed a new partnership with Hellas Verona as part of the Italian side’s HV Academy project. The collaboration is aimed at the development of young football talent in Ghana while cultivating cultural exchange between both footballing communities. Operating out of Obuasi in Ghana’s Ashanti Region, Desire FC launched its Youth Sector in 2016 and has facilitated growth in it’s development programme. The institute has teams from the Under-15 through to the Under-21 level. The results have been positive as several of the academy’s emerging talents have received call-ups to regional representative teams. The Hellas Verona alliance promotes the development of the academy’s players and enhances the pathway from Ghanaian youth football to the Italian Game. Desire Fc President Sammy Appiah and Sporting Director Salvatore Zito visited Hellas Verona’s headquarters where a Desire FC shirt was officially handed over to the Italian club on September 30. Appiah expressed his happiness upon visiting Verona and pointed out the connection between Ghanaian players and the city. “I am a great fan of Italian football and I have followed Verona over the years. items.title: Labone robbery case adjourned to October 22 as prosecution prepares supplementary statements
items.description: The trial of Augustine Okechuku Maazi, the first accused in the alleged Labone robbery case, has been adjourned to October 22, 2026, after the prosecution indicated that it intends to file supplementary witness statements. The prosecution told the Accra Circuit Court that the case was expected to proceed with a case management conference on Tuesday but encountered difficulties serving the defence with the necessary documents. It also informed the court that it needed to file additional witness statements before the matter could proceed. The defence, meanwhile, sought bail for Mr Maazi, arguing that he had already spent considerable time in custody. The court, however, declined to entertain the oral bail application and directed the defence to file a formal application at the next hearing. Mr Maazi is facing eight counts, including conspiracy to commit crime to wit robbery, attempted robbery and robbery. He has pleaded not guilty to the charges. The case stems from a police operation on August 13, 2026, after intelligence indicated that a suspected robbery syndicate was preparing to target banks in the Labone area of Accra. Police said the targeted banks included GCB Bank, Ecobank and Zenith Bank. One suspect, identified as Mr Maazi, was arrested, while two other suspected accomplices were killed during an exchange of gunfire with police. Prosecutors have also alleged that investigations linked Mr Maazi and five other suspects to a series of robberies in Tema, Spintex and Labone between May and August 13, 2026. The prosecution further alleged that the group operated across Ghana’s borders, including Togo and Côte d’Ivoire, while investigators continue to trace other suspected accomplices who remain at large. The defence’s formal bail application is therefore expected to be considered when the case returns to court on October 22.
